GAN supplies B2B online casino and sports betting technology: its GameSTACK platform-as-a-service plus the Coolbet sportsbook acquired in 2021, which it runs directly in Europe and Latin America. The iGaming platform powers real-money and social casino operators in regulated US states, with customers including large casino groups. Revenue comes from platform fees, revenue share and B2C betting income. Founded in 2002 and listed on Nasdaq (GAN) since 2020; Sega Sammy agreed to acquire it in 2025. Little consumer awareness of GAN itself, though Coolbet has some regional presence in the Nordics and Estonia. Gambling sponsorship is restricted in many F1 markets.

Guangdong Guanghua Sci-Tech is a Chinese specialty chemicals and electronic materials maker based in Shantou, best known for high-purity chemicals used in the electronics industry, such as solvents, acids and other wet process chemicals for printed circuit boards, semiconductors and display panels. Its customers are electronics manufacturers rather than consumers, and it sells under the Guanghua name. It is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (stock code 002741) and has a long operating history in Guangdong, with additional production sites in other Chinese provinces. B2B supplier with essentially no consumer brand awareness outside China, so limited sponsorship relevance.

Marubi Biotechnology is a Chinese beauty and skincare company headquartered in Guangzhou, owner of the Marubi (丸美) brand of eye care and anti-aging skincare, plus the Lianfeng and Lian Jia Li mass-market brands and the Lady's brand. Products are sold through online channels such as Tmall, Douyin and JD as well as cosmetics counters and specialty stores, mostly to Chinese women, with revenue coming from product sales. Founded in 2002 and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (stock code 603983) in 2019. It is a recognised domestic consumer brand with heavy celebrity and social media marketing, but little international profile.

Just Dial is an Indian local search and business listing platform that lets consumers find and contact local merchants and service providers by phone, website, mobile app and WhatsApp. It lists millions of businesses and earns revenue mainly from advertising and subscription packages paid by small and medium businesses, as well as verified-listing and lead-generation services. Founded in 1996 by V. S. S. Mani as a phone-based directory, it went public in India in 2013 (BSE/NSE: JUSTDIAL), and in 2021 Reliance Retail bought a controlling stake. Strong consumer brand recognition across India, with a well-known jingle and the 'Search Ke Baap' campaigns; low relevance outside India.

Just Eat Takeaway.com was a leading online food delivery marketplace connecting restaurants and customers, formed in 2020 when Takeaway.com merged with Just Eat plc. Operating in the UK, Netherlands, Germany, Canada and other markets, it earned commission on orders and delivery fees from restaurants, and had Grubhub in the US until 2021 when it was sold. It was listed on Euronext Amsterdam (TKWY) and the London Stock Exchange. In 2025 Prosus completed a roughly 4.1 billion euro takeover, delisting the company. Highly visible consumer brand in Europe with heavy TV and sports advertising, including past football sponsorship, so a familiar sponsor profile.

Jyoti CNC Automation is an Indian maker of computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools, including turning centres, vertical and horizontal machining centres and multi-axis machines, sold under the Jyoti and Hi-Tech brands. Customers are industrial manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, defence, medical and general engineering, and revenue comes from machine sales, spares and service. Founded in 1991 and operating from Rajkot, Gujarat, one of Asia's larger CNC makers, with exports to Europe, North America and Asia and a European subsidiary in Germany/France. Listed on Indian exchanges (NSE/BSE: JYOTICNC) after a 2024 IPO. B2B industrial brand, with low public awareness but strong standing within manufacturing.

Metals Acquisition Corp was a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) set up in 2021 to buy a metals and mining business. In 2023 it completed its deal to acquire the CSA Copper Mine in Cobar, New South Wales, Australia, from Glencore, and renamed itself Metals Acquisition Limited (NYSE and ASX: MAC), now a copper producer with underground operations producing roughly 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes of copper a year. Customers are copper smelters and traders, so it is a pure B2B commodity producer with no consumer profile. The Fort Worth, Texas, office reflects its US management and shell origin, while operations are in Australia.

National Finance is an Omani financial services company based in Muscat, providing consumer and business finance such as personal loans, vehicle and asset financing and Islamic-style finance products to Omani residents and companies. It earns income from interest and fees on its lending book and is listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange (MSM). It operates as a non-bank lender alongside Oman's retail banks. Regional financial brand with some local visibility in Oman but little recognition elsewhere. Sponsorship fit is mostly limited to the Omani market; some regional lenders do back sport and events.

Ooma sells cloud-based phone and communications services. Its Ooma Office product is a business VoIP phone system with virtual receptionist, video meetings and mobile app, aimed at small businesses, while Ooma Telo and Ooma Residential offer low-cost home phone service. It also owns the Ooma Enterprise and AirDial products (emergency and POTS-replacement lines) and acquired Voxter, 2600Hz and OnSIP. Revenue is mainly subscriptions plus device sales. Founded in 2004, it listed on the NYSE (OOMA) in 2015 and serves hundreds of thousands of business and residential customers, mostly in the US and Canada. Moderate consumer name recognition in North America, with no known major sports sponsorship history.

Queensland Pacific Metals is an Australian-listed battery metals developer planning to process nickel and cobalt laterite ore from New Caledonia and elsewhere at a hydrometallurgical refinery in Townsville, Queensland, producing battery-grade nickel sulphate and cobalt sulphate, plus ammonium sulphate by-products. The target customers are lithium-ion battery cathode makers and electric vehicle supply chains. It is listed on the ASX (QPM) and has been working on its Townsville Energy Chemicals Hub project, with Australian government support. It is pre-revenue and project-stage, a pure B2B company with minimal public brand awareness, so brand sponsorship relevance is limited.

Rottneros is a Swedish pulp producer operating two mills, Vallvik and Rottneros, making chemical (sulphate) pulp and chemimechanical pulp (CTMP) from Nordic softwood and spruce. Customers are paper and board makers and manufacturers of tissue, specialty papers, filters and packaging, mainly in Europe, which buy it as an input. Revenue comes from pulp sales and it also sells energy and by-products. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and the Oslo Stock Exchange (ROT). It supplies B2B materials with no consumer brand and is not a typical sponsor.

Sage Microelectronique, based in Xiaoshan, Zhejiang, appears to be a Chinese electronics and information technology company, likely a semiconductor or integrated circuit business serving electronics manufacturers, but I cannot confirm its products, listing or ownership. Crunchbase tags it as electronics and information technology with a large CNY funding round in 2019. It is most likely a B2B component supplier with no consumer brand and no known sponsorship activity. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Sprout Social sells cloud software that helps companies manage social media: publishing and scheduling, a unified inbox, listening and analytics, employee advocacy, and influencer marketing tools. Customers are marketers, agencies and customer-care teams at businesses of all sizes, which pay recurring subscriptions, with roughly 30,000 paying customers and revenue above 400 million dollars. Founded in 2010 in Chicago and listed on Nasdaq (SPT) since 2019. It has acquired Simply Measured, Tagger and NewsWhip. B2B software brand with moderate awareness among marketers but little with the general public. A natural fit for brand-activation and content storytelling deals around event sponsorship.

Toyo Solar, a Vietnam-based subsidiary of the Japanese-owned Toyo Co., Ltd., manufactures solar cells and modules at a large plant in Quang Ninh province, exporting mainly to the United States market. Its products are high-efficiency crystalline silicon cells and modules for utility-scale and commercial solar projects, sold B2B to developers and module assemblers. Toyo Co. is listed on Nasdaq (TOYO), having gone public via a 2024 IPO. Part of the global shift of solar manufacturing out of China into Southeast Asia, with multi-gigawatt capacity. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand, so limited sponsorship use beyond energy-transition messaging.

Unipar Carbocloro is a Brazilian producer of chlor-alkali chemicals and related products, making chlorine, caustic soda, PVC resin, sodium hypochlorite and hydrochloric acid at plants in Cubatao and Cajati in Sao Paulo state. It sells to industrial customers in water treatment, plastics, construction, pulp and paper, textiles and other sectors, and is among the leading Brazilian producers of PVC. The company is part of the Unipar group, which is listed on B3 in Sao Paulo (UNIP3/UNIP6). B2B chemical manufacturer with no consumer brand awareness, so unlikely to be an F1 sponsor.

Zillow Group runs the largest US online real estate marketplace, with Zillow, Trulia, StreetEasy, HotPads and Out East brands. Consumers search homes for sale and rent and see Zestimate valuations, while revenue comes from advertising and lead fees from agents, rental listings, and mortgage products via Zillow Home Loans. It exited the iBuying business in 2021. Founded in 2006 and listed on Nasdaq (Z, ZG), Zillow has roughly 200 million monthly users and revenue of about 2 billion dollars. It is a household name in the US with heavy brand advertising and some sports marketing, so a plausible North American sponsor.

Website Pros is an Australian digital agency based in Carrum Downs, Victoria, building and hosting websites and e-commerce stores for small and medium businesses and providing related online marketing services such as SEO and search advertising. Customers are local Australian companies buying website design, hosting and ongoing marketing packages. I do not have reliable details on its size or ownership, so the description rests mainly on the Crunchbase categories of e-commerce and internet. Likely a small, private B2B services provider with local rather than national brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Arcvideo Technology is a video technology company with offices in San Jose and China, providing software for video processing, such as transcoding, cloud video platforms, AI-based video analysis and live broadcast production. Customers include broadcasters, telecom operators, online video platforms and media companies, who pay licences and project fees. It raised sizeable funding in China and is a B2B software supplier known mainly to media-technology buyers, with little consumer awareness. Its sponsorship relevance is limited to media-technology storytelling.

BCP Investment Corporation is a US business development company (BDC), a listed closed-end fund that lends to and invests in middle-market private companies, mainly through senior secured loans. It is externally managed by an affiliate of BC Partners and was formed through the Portman Ridge and Logan Ridge combination. Revenue comes from interest on its loan portfolio, and it pays dividends to shareholders. It trades on Nasdaq. This is a financial vehicle rather than an operating brand, with no consumer awareness, so it has little relevance for brand sponsorship.

Bo Rui Tong Yun is a Beijing-based Chinese artificial intelligence company whose Crunchbase tags point to AI, data and software services. I do not recognise it well enough to describe its products, customers or ownership with confidence. It appears to be a technology provider selling AI-enabled services to enterprise or government customers in China, funded by sizeable private or public financing. Brand awareness is likely confined to its B2B niche. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Borregaard is a Norwegian biorefinery that turns sustainably harvested wood into specialty chemicals: lignin-based binders and dispersants (Borresperse, Vanisperse), vanillin for flavours, cellulose fibres (Exilva microfibrillar cellulose) and bioethanol. It runs its main plant in Sarpsborg and sells to construction, agriculture, food, pharma and battery makers worldwide, with export markets across Europe, Asia and the Americas. Revenue is roughly 3 to 4 billion Norwegian kroner. Founded in 1889 and listed on Oslo Bors (BRG). B2B ingredient supplier whose brand is little known to consumers, though its sustainability story fits climate-focused partnerships.

Buhler Industries is a Canadian agricultural equipment maker, based in Winnipeg, producing tractors under the Versatile brand (four-wheel-drive articulated tractors for large farms), plus sprayers, swathers and other implements, with Farm King and Allied attachments. It sells to farmers through a dealer network in North America, and also supplies tractors internationally. Owned by Russian farm machinery group Rostselmash from 2007. A recognised farm-machinery brand in North America, but sales run through dealers and its audience is agricultural, with low general consumer reach.

CARE Ratings is one of India's major credit rating agencies, based in Mumbai, rating bonds, bank loans, commercial paper and companies' debt for corporates, banks and infrastructure issuers. It also offers advisory and analytical services and operates in India, Africa (via CARE Ratings Africa) and Nepal. Revenue comes from rating fees. It was set up in 1993 and promoted by IDBI Bank, Canara Bank and other institutions, and is listed on BSE and NSE (CARERATING). A B2B institution known mainly to financial professionals and issuers rather than consumers, so it has low public brand visibility.

Chargeurs is a French industrial and luxury-linked group that was founded in 1872 and is listed on Euronext Paris. It runs several businesses: Chargeurs Protective Films (surface protection films for metals and plastics), Chargeurs Fashion Technologies (interlinings used by apparel makers), Chargeurs Luxury Materials (wool top for luxury suiting, via the Leach and Lainière de Picardie operations) and PCC Chargeurs Museum Solutions. Customers are manufacturers and luxury brands, with revenue of about 700 million euros and operations globally. B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness, though the luxury link may appeal to some partners.

Corero Network Security provides DDoS (distributed denial of service) protection, with its SmartWall appliances and SecureWatch analytics detecting and blocking attacks in real time at network edges. Customers are internet service providers, hosting and cloud companies, and enterprises, who buy hardware, software subscriptions and managed services. Corero is headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts, with its engineering roots in the UK, and is listed on the London AIM market (CNS). Revenue is around 25 to 30 million dollars. B2B cybersecurity vendor with low consumer awareness, though technical partnerships in motorsport are conceivable.

drugstore.com was a US online pharmacy and health and beauty retailer, selling pharmacy items, vitamins, personal care, skincare and cosmetics, with sister sites such as beauty.com. It sold directly to consumers online, earning product margins. Founded in 1998 in Bellevue, Washington, with early backing from Amazon, it listed on Nasdaq (DSCM) in 1999 and was acquired by Walgreens in 2011 for about 409 million dollars, after which the site was folded into Walgreens' online business. A known e-commerce brand in the US in the 2000s but no longer operating independently.

Elixirr is a London-based consulting firm that works with large corporate clients and private-equity-backed businesses on strategy, digital transformation, innovation and growth, through Elixirr Consulting and acquired practices such as Insigniam and Elixirr Digital. It follows a model of entrepreneurial partner-led firms sharing one brand, with a workforce in the hundreds and revenue above 100 million pounds. Listed on London's AIM (ELIX) in 2021, with clients across the UK, US and Europe. Professional-services brand known mostly to executives and procurement teams, with limited consumer visibility.

Entegris is a US supplier of advanced materials and process solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, including filters, chemical delivery systems, high-purity chemicals and gases, specialty coatings, and wafer and chip containers. Customers are the chipmakers and equipment makers, such as TSMC, Intel and Samsung, which buy products and replacements repeatedly. Revenue is several billion dollars, after the 2022 acquisition of CMC Materials. Listed on Nasdaq (ENTG) and headquartered in Billerica, Massachusetts, with a global footprint including Asia. B2B industrial brand with no consumer presence and low general public awareness.

Entel is a major Chilean telecommunications operator, providing mobile, fixed broadband, data centre, cloud, IT and digital services to consumers and businesses in Chile and Peru. It operates a large 4G and 5G mobile network and enterprise solutions. Founded in 1964 as Empresa Nacional de Telecomunicaciones and listed on the Santiago stock exchange (ENTEL), it has millions of subscribers and is one of Chile's best-known telecom brands. Active in sports and entertainment sponsorship in Chile, notably football and music events, so it understands brand sponsorship.

Finjan Holdings was a US cybersecurity company based in California that developed web security technology and later focused on licensing its patent portfolio, earning royalty and settlement income from technology companies. It descended from the original Finjan Software, an Israeli-founded web security firm, and was listed on Nasdaq (FNJN). In 2020 it was acquired by Fortress Investment Group's affiliate in a deal worth around 40 million dollars and was delisted. It had little consumer awareness and no longer operates as an independent listed brand.

Fusion Fuel Green is a green hydrogen technology company, originally based in Portugal, developing electrolysers that produce hydrogen from solar power for use in industry and mobility. Its main product has been the HEVO modular electrolyser systems, sold to project developers and industrial customers, mostly in Europe and the Middle East. It listed on Nasdaq (HTOO) via a SPAC merger in 2020 and has faced financial difficulty and restructuring. Small, B2B, with minimal brand awareness. Its fit with F1 would be sustainability messaging, but the commercial scale is modest.

GHL Systems is a Malaysian payments company providing electronic payment terminals, merchant acquiring, e-payments, and loyalty and transaction processing services for merchants across Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines and other Southeast Asian countries. Revenue comes from device sales, transaction fees and managed services. It was listed on Bursa Malaysia (GHLSYS) and was taken over by Global Payments of the US, which acquired it in 2022 and delisted it. B2B payments brand known to retailers and banks in Southeast Asia, with little consumer-facing profile.

Glaston is a Finnish technology company making glass processing machines, especially for tempering, laminating and bending architectural, automotive and appliance glass, and offers upgrades, spare parts and service plus software. Its customers are glass processors serving construction, automotive and solar. It operates in Europe, North America and Asia, has several hundred employees, and revenue of roughly 200 million euros. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (GLA1V), with a history linked to the Finnish Tamglass business. B2B equipment maker with little consumer awareness, so its sponsorship relevance is limited.

Hi-Tech Pipes is an Indian maker of steel pipes and tubes, including electric resistance welded pipes, galvanised pipes, structural hollow sections and solar mounting structures, with plants in several Indian states. It sells to construction, infrastructure, automotive, agriculture and engineering customers via distributors, and generates revenue from steel product sales. Based in the Delhi region, it is listed on BSE and NSE (HITECH). B2B industrial brand with minimal consumer recognition, mostly known in Indian trade channels.

Hongli Zhihui Group, based in Guangzhou, is a Chinese company involved in electronics components and marketing services, with a sizeable yuan funding round. I cannot reliably describe its products or customers, but it appears to be a B2B electronics and marketing services business serving Chinese manufacturers and advertisers, with little consumer visibility. Crunchbase tags it as electronics and marketing. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Huuuge Games is a Polish mobile games developer and publisher best known for free-to-play social casino titles such as Huuuge Casino, Billionaire Casino and Spades Plus, plus a few mid-core games. Revenue comes from in-app purchases and advertising by players, primarily in the US and Europe, with millions of monthly active users. Founded in 2012 and based in Warsaw, it is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (HUG), with offices in Berlin and Tel Aviv. Consumer-facing in app stores but not a household name, and social casino marketing is sensitive in some sponsorship contexts.

iPass was a US provider of managed Wi-Fi and mobility services, offering software and a global roaming network that let enterprise workers and operators connect to Wi-Fi hotspots securely, via its Open Mobile platform. Customers were large enterprises and telecom operators paying subscriptions and usage fees. Founded in 1996 and listed on Nasdaq (IPAS), it was acquired by Pareteum in 2019. It had little consumer awareness and no longer operates as a standalone brand, making it irrelevant as a current sponsor.

Ladenburg Thalmann Financial Services was a US diversified financial services holding company, with independent broker-dealer networks (Securities America, Triad Advisors, Investacorp, KMS Financial Services), plus insurance brokerage and asset management. It served financial advisers and their retail clients, earning commissions and advisory fees, and was headquartered in Miami, Florida, with roots in an old New York investment bank. Listed on NYSE American (LTS), it was acquired by Advisor Group in 2020 in a deal worth roughly 1.3 billion dollars. B2B within financial advice, with little brand awareness among consumers.

Luoyang Northglass Technology is a Chinese glass processing and equipment company in Luoyang, Henan, known for glass deep-processing machinery such as tempering furnaces, laminating lines and related equipment and services for architectural and industrial glass makers. Customers are glass processors in China and export markets. It is listed on a mainland Chinese exchange and grew out of a long-standing Chinese glass industry business. B2B equipment maker with no consumer brand awareness and very limited relevance for sponsorship.

Mattersight was a US analytics software company that used behavioural analytics to match customers with the best contact-centre agents based on personality and communication style, helping call centres in banking, telecom, insurance and healthcare improve satisfaction and sales. It was based in Chicago, sold cloud software under subscription, and was listed on Nasdaq (MATR). It was acquired by NICE Systems in 2018 for about 94 million dollars. Little consumer awareness, and no longer exists as an independent brand.

Mitra Adiperkasa is one of Indonesia's largest lifestyle and fashion retailers, operating and franchising international brands such as Zara, Marks & Spencer, Starbucks, Burger King, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Lego, Foot Locker and Sports Station through hundreds of stores across the country. Customers are mass and premium Indonesian consumers, and it earns retail and food-and-beverage revenue. Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (MAPI), founded in 1995. Its stores are visible in malls across Indonesia, although it is a retail operator rather than a single consumer brand of its own.

Modular Medical is a US medical device company developing a small, simple insulin pump for people with diabetes, called the Pivot pump, designed to be lower cost and easier to use with a disposable patch and reusable controller. Its customers are people with diabetes and prescribers, and it targets the US market. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (MODD), it is still at the commercial launch stage with small revenue. Little public brand awareness. Sponsorship fit would be more about health and wellness than visibility.

NSTC is a Beijing-based Chinese financial technology and information services business. Crunchbase tags it as finance and information technology, and shows a sizeable yuan funding round. I cannot confirm exactly what it does or who owns it. It is likely a B2B software or financial information supplier to institutions in China, with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

ON24 is a US software company whose cloud platform runs webinars, virtual events, and personalised digital experiences, providing engagement analytics and lead data to B2B marketers. Its customers include enterprises in technology, financial services and healthcare, who pay subscriptions. Founded in 1998, it went public on the NYSE (ONTF) in 2021 and had revenue of roughly 150 to 200 million dollars. In 2025 it agreed to be acquired by Cvent. B2B software brand known to marketers, with little consumer awareness.

Ourpalm is a Chinese mobile game developer and publisher, listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board (300315), known for publishing and operating mobile games in China and abroad, including titles built on licensed film and TV properties, plus game distribution and developer services. Revenue comes from in-game purchases and licensing. Founded in 2004 and based in Beijing. Consumer-facing games with moderate awareness in Chinese mobile gaming, little elsewhere. A gaming company could fit F1 fan engagement.

PowerFleet is a US provider of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions for asset management: devices and software that track and manage vehicles, trailers, forklifts, containers and industrial equipment. Its products include Unity, Pointer and Fleet Complete lines, serving logistics, retail, transport and manufacturing customers on subscription plans and with RFID hardware. Based in New Jersey, with operations in Israel and Brazil, and listed on Nasdaq (PWFL). Acquired Fleet Complete in 2024. B2B brand with limited public awareness.

PT Nippon Indosari Corpindo is an Indonesian packaged bakery company making Sari Roti, the country's leading branded packaged bread, along with buns, cakes and pastries, sold in supermarkets, minimarkets and traditional shops across Indonesia. It operates large factories in Java and elsewhere in the country and sells through an extensive distribution network. Founded in 1995 and listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (ROTI), it has Japanese partners such as Pasco Shikishima in its background. Strong mass-consumer brand with everyday recognition, a plausible sponsor of events in Indonesia.

QD Laser is a Japanese company that develops semiconductor lasers based on quantum dot technology, with products for optical communications, consumer retinal projection eyewear (laser eyewear for low-vision users), laser sensing and industrial uses. It spun out of Fujitsu and the University of Tokyo, and is based in Kawasaki and Yokohama. It is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth market (6613). Customers include equipment makers and, for its laser eyewear, consumers and clinics. Small and mostly known in photonics, with little mainstream brand awareness.

QuantGroup is a Chinese quantitative investment and financial data technology company based in Beijing, tagged by Crunchbase as big data, database and finance. It appears to provide data, databases and quantitative research tools to investors and financial institutions, but I cannot confirm detailed products or ownership. Probably a B2B data and analytics provider serving funds and institutions in China, with little consumer presence. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Safeguard Scientifics is a US holding company that provides capital and strategic support to early-stage technology businesses in healthcare technology, fintech and software, taking minority and majority stakes. Its past holdings included Clarient, Alliance Consulting, Sanchez Computer Associates and Prophet 21. It was founded in 1953 and is based in Radnor, Pennsylvania, and listed on the NYSE and later OTC (SFE). It earns returns from selling its stakes. Little consumer awareness, and it is a financial vehicle rather than a brand, so not a typical sponsor.

Security and Intelligence Services (India) Ltd, or SIS, is an Indian security and facility services group providing manned guarding, cash logistics, electronic security systems, and facility management and housekeeping to corporate and government clients, and also operates in Australia and the UK, with a workforce of hundreds of thousands. Founded in 1985, it is listed on BSE and NSE (SIS). B2B services brand, with visibility on security guard uniforms across Indian offices and malls but little consumer-facing marketing.

Sunmi Technology develops smart commercial devices, notably Android-based point-of-sale terminals, handheld scanners, kiosks, receipt printers and AI-powered retail hardware, serving restaurants, retailers, logistics and payment companies in China and abroad. Its customers include payment providers and merchants in dozens of countries, with revenue from hardware plus software services. Founded in 2013 in Shanghai, with a Singapore headquarters shown here, and backed by Tencent and others, but not listed. B2B brand with limited consumer visibility, although its devices are widely seen in shops.

Thryv is a US small-business marketing and software company, known for the former Yellow Pages directory business (Dex Media) which it reshaped into SaaS. Its Thryv platform bundles CRM, appointment booking, invoicing, payments and marketing services for local service businesses, plus Marketing Services and the legacy print and online directories. It is headquartered in Dallas and listed on Nasdaq (THRY). Customers are small and medium businesses across the US, and revenue is around 1 billion dollars. Moderate brand awareness among small business owners, little among the general public.

Twenty First Century Aerospace Technology is a Chinese company in Beijing's Haidian district, tagged by Crunchbase as big data and information services. The name suggests aerospace and satellite applications, but I cannot verify its details. The yuan-denominated funding suggests it is a venture-style or listed technology business serving government and enterprise customers, and its brand awareness is probably limited to its niche. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

VirnetX is a US internet security and patent licensing company that developed secure communications technology (Gabriel Collaboration Suite and VirnetX One), but earns most of its revenue from patent litigation against Apple, with large court verdicts and settlements. It is based in Zephyr Cove, Nevada, was founded in 2005, and is listed on NYSE American (VHC). The business depends on court outcomes more than on products, and there is almost no consumer brand awareness. It is not a typical sponsor.

Zenvia is a Brazilian customer-communications platform that helps companies engage consumers through WhatsApp, SMS, voice, RCS, chatbots and CRM tools, in a cloud platform. Customers are large enterprises and mid-size companies in retail, finance and services across Latin America. Based in Sao Paulo, it listed on Nasdaq (ZENV) in 2021 and has acquired companies such as Sensedata, Movidesk and D1. B2B technology brand with little consumer visibility; its marketing is mostly business-focused. It has sizeable revenue in Brazilian reais and is one of the region's larger communication-API providers.

ADLINK Technology is a Taiwanese maker of embedded computing and edge AI hardware, offering industrial computers, boards, modules, data acquisition, test and measurement equipment and gateways used in automation, medical, defence, transportation and communications. Customers are industrial OEMs and system integrators worldwide, with offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Founded in 1995 and based in Taoyuan, it is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (6166). B2B brand known mainly to engineers, with little consumer awareness.

Amethystum is a Chinese data storage company based in Meizhou, Guangdong, which makes enterprise storage hardware and software systems, such as all-flash and hybrid arrays, for big data and cloud customers. It supplies government, finance and education customers and is listed on the Shanghai STAR Market (688086). It is a B2B infrastructure vendor with limited public brand awareness outside enterprise IT circles in China, and no known sponsorship activity of any kind.

Antaitech is a Chinese information services technology company based in Hefei, Anhui, with a funding round reported in yuan. I do not recognise its product line well enough to state its customers or ownership with confidence. It is probably a B2B technology supplier to government or industrial customers in China, with little consumer awareness. Crunchbase tags it only as information services. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Artificial Solutions is a Swedish conversational AI software company, with its Teneo platform for building virtual assistants and chatbots that understand natural language across voice and text channels. Customers include large telecoms, banks, car makers and retailers in Europe and the US, who pay for licences and professional services. Founded in 2001 in Stockholm, it raised venture and growth funding and now operates under the Teneo name. B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness, though known among conversational AI buyers.

BASE is a Japanese e-commerce enablement company whose BASE service lets individuals and small businesses open an online shop in minutes with no upfront fee, and which also runs the PAY.JP payment service and the Pay ID shopping app and wallet. Revenue comes from transaction fees and optional paid apps, with over a million shops created. Founded in 2012 and based in Tokyo, it listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth market (4477) in 2020. Strong awareness among Japanese sellers and creators, and moderate among shoppers, and it has run TV and online advertising campaigns in Japan.

Computer Age Management Services (CAMS) is India's largest registrar and transfer agent for mutual funds, handling investor records, transactions, KYC and servicing for fund houses that together manage the majority of Indian mutual fund assets. It also offers insurance repository, payment aggregator and digital services via platforms like CAMSPay and CAMSonline. Customers are asset managers and regulators, and revenue comes from per-folio and per-transaction fees. Promoted by HDFC Bank and later partly owned by Great Hill Partners, it listed on BSE and NSE (CAMS) in 2020. B2B, with low consumer awareness.

Dalen is a Suzhou-based Chinese electronics company, with hardware products that Crunchbase tags as electronics and hardware. I cannot reliably identify its exact products, customers or ownership. It appears to be a B2B electronics or components maker serving device manufacturers, with modest disclosed funding. It has little consumer brand awareness outside its niche, and I know of no sponsorship activity. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Das Security, based in Hangzhou, is a Chinese cybersecurity and data security company tagged as big data, hardware and security. It sells security products such as network and data security appliances and related services to government, finance and enterprise customers in China. I cannot confirm product names or ownership with confidence. B2B security supplier with little public brand awareness beyond Chinese enterprise IT. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Dixon Technologies is India's largest home-grown electronics manufacturing services company, making televisions, washing machines, LED lighting, mobile phones and security cameras, largely for other brands under contract, including Samsung, Xiaomi, Motorola and Philips, plus its own Padget and Dixon labels. Customers are consumer electronics brands, with revenue running into several billion dollars on production-linked incentive schemes. Founded in 1993 and based in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, it is listed on the NSE and BSE (DIXON). B2B manufacturer with low consumer brand awareness despite its huge production volumes.

TeraView is a Cambridge, UK, company that makes terahertz imaging and spectroscopy equipment, which uses terahertz light to inspect materials, coatings, pharmaceuticals and semiconductor devices without damaging them. The Container Store is a US specialty retailer of storage and organisation products, selling custom closet systems (Elfa), containers, shelving, and home organisation items through around 100 stores and online. High-visibility mass-market consumer brand, widely seen across the country.

Aiming is a Japanese mobile game developer and publisher in Tokyo, known for smartphone titles such as Dragon Quest Tact, Million Arthur and the MMORPG Dungeon Link and Tower of Magic, creating games under licences from companies like Square Enix. Ashland is a US specialty chemicals company making additives and ingredients for pharmaceuticals, personal care, food, coatings and construction, with products such as cellulose ethers, vinyl pyrrolidones and Natrosol thickeners. Roughly 4,000 employees, with revenue around 2 billion dollars and the headquarters now moved from Kentucky to Delaware. B2B ingredient brand with little consumer awareness.

Ceinsys Tech is an Indian technology and engineering services company in Nagpur providing geospatial services, GIS, software, engineering design and IoT solutions for utilities, water, transport and government clients, including digital mapping and smart city projects. B2B services brand with limited consumer awareness, so not an obvious sponsorship target, although it has regional government relationships.

Chesswood Group is a Canadian specialty finance company that, through Pawnee Leasing and Tandem Finance in the US, provides equipment leasing and financing for small businesses, with leases for items like trucks, restaurant gear and medical equipment, sourced via vendors and brokers. A B2B lender with no consumer brand awareness.

Confidence Group (Confidence Petroleum India) is a Nagpur-based Indian company in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) business, bottling and distributing cooking gas cylinders, building LPG autogas stations and manufacturing cylinders and valves, with additional ventures in CNG and energy equipment. B2B brand known in legal tech circles, with little consumer awareness.

Customers are Indian Railways, defence agencies and industrial buyers. Founded in 1977 and based in Hyderabad, it is listed on NSE and BSE (HBLENGINE). B2B industrial supplier with little consumer awareness.

Heidmar is a Greek-based commercial manager of oil tanker pools, with fleets of crude and product tankers operated for ship owners, and also provides trading and logistics services in the shipping industry. Indorama Ventures is a Thai-based global petrochemical company and the world's largest producer of PET resin for bottles, plus polyester fibres and yarns and ethylene oxide derivatives, with plants across Asia, Europe, the Americas and Africa. It is a subsidiary of the Lohia family-led Indorama group and is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (IVL). Revenue is above 15 billion dollars. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness.

IP Group is a UK-listed intellectual property commercialisation and venture company that invests in spinouts from universities and technology businesses, including past stakes in Oxford Nanopore, Featurespace and Hinge Health. Italian Exhibition Group (IEG) is Italy's leading trade fair and exhibition organiser, running events such as Ecomondo, Key Energy, TTG Travel Experience, SIA Hospitality Design, Vicenza Oro and the Rimini Wellness fitness show, as well as operating the Rimini and Vicenza exhibition centres and a congress business. Customers are exhibitors, trade visitors and event organisers, and revenue comes from stand space, tickets and services. Jieshun Technology is a Shenzhen-based Chinese smart parking and traffic technology company that makes parking lot management systems, license-plate recognition cameras, barriers, access control and smart city parking platforms and services. Founded in the 1990s and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002609). B2B brand known in the Chinese parking and security sector, with limited consumer awareness.

MonotaRO is a Japanese e-commerce company selling industrial and maintenance supplies, with more than 20 million products such as tools, safety gear, factory consumables and office supplies, to small and medium manufacturers, construction firms and tradespeople through an online catalogue. Monte Carlo Fashions is an Indian apparel company, based in Ludhiana, Punjab, best known for woollen and winter clothing such as sweaters, jackets and thermals, plus cotton, denim and casual wear for men, women and kids under the Monte Carlo and Rock.it brands. It sells through exclusive brand outlets, multi-brand stores and e-commerce. Founded in 1984 as part of the Oswal Woollen Mills group, and listed on the NSE and BSE (MONTECARLO). Recognised consumer brand in North India with strong retail presence.

Nanotech Security is a Canadian company based in Burnaby, British Columbia, that develops nanotechnology-based optical security features to protect banknotes, ID documents and brands, including its KolourOptik nano-optic films, and supplies them to central banks and security printers. Revenue comes from licensing, products and development fees. It was listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (NTS). It is a B2B niche supplier with no consumer brand awareness. I cannot confirm its current ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Net1 UEPS Technologies (now Lesaka Technologies) is a South African fintech company that runs payment and financial services for unbanked and underbanked consumers and small businesses: social grant payments through its UEPS technology, prepaid airtime, bill payments, lending and insurance, and merchant services via Cash Connect and Kazang. Based in Johannesburg and listed on Nasdaq (LSAK, formerly UEPS) and the JSE. Renamed Lesaka in 2021. Customers are millions of low-income South Africans and thousands of merchants. Some local brand recognition in South Africa through its payment and merchant services, little elsewhere.

Pakka is an Indian sustainable packaging and paper business in Uttar Pradesh that makes paper, paperboard and packaging products from sugarcane bagasse, including food-grade bagasse tableware and paper for printing and writing. It exports bagasse-based packaging to Europe and North America, with customers in food service and consumer goods industries. It is listed on Indian exchanges. It is an eco-focused B2B supplier with a growing sustainability profile and little consumer awareness, so any sponsor use would be about green credentials.

Paradox Interactive is a Swedish video game publisher and developer known for grand strategy and management games such as Europa Universalis, Crusader Kings, Hearts of Iron, Stellaris, Cities: Skylines and Surviving Mars, plus the Magicka and Vampire: The Masquerade franchises. It sells PC and console games, DLC and expansions, mostly to adult gamers worldwide, with revenue around 2 billion Swedish kronor. Founded in 1999 and based in Stockholm, and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (PDX). Strong brand among PC strategy gamers, with limited mainstream awareness.

PayRight is an Australian fintech in Sydney that offers buy-now-pay-later and instalment financing, with its PayRight product letting consumers pay for purchases, such as medical, veterinary and home services, in fixed instalments. It reports roughly 27 million dollars of funding and sells through merchants and healthcare providers. Private and relatively small, with consumer exposure mainly through partner merchants. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Prosafe is a Norwegian offshore accommodation company, with semi-submersible rigs known as floatels that house workers beside oil and gas platforms, mostly in the North Sea and Brazil. B2B offshore service provider with no consumer profile, and little relevance for sponsorship.

Radisys was a US telecom equipment and software company in Hillsboro, Oregon, that made network function virtualisation software, media servers and embedded platforms such as the DCEngine data centre hardware sold to telcos including Reliance Jio and AT&T and cable operators. Founded in 1987 and listed on Nasdaq (RSYS), it was acquired by Reliance Industries in 2018 for about 74 million dollars and operates as a Reliance subsidiary. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Safie is a Japanese cloud video recording and AI analytics company that sells cloud-connected security cameras and the Safie service, which lets businesses and homes watch, store and analyse video through apps, used for stores, construction sites, factories and homes. Known in Japan to business buyers, with modest consumer awareness.

Shanghang is a Guangzhou-based Chinese cloud data services and information technology company, with funding of around 223 million yuan. Sigma Labs, now Sigma Additive Solutions, is a US software company whose PrintRite3D quality assurance system monitors metal 3D printing in real time to detect defects, for aerospace, defence, medical and industrial customers using additive manufacturing. Customers are 3D printer users and makers, who pay for software licences and subscriptions. Based in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and listed on Nasdaq (SGLB), it later merged with NextTrip in 2024. Small B2B software brand, known to additive manufacturing engineers, with no consumer awareness.

Teledyne FLIR is a thermal imaging, infrared camera and sensing business, part of Teledyne Technologies since its 2021 acquisition of FLIR Systems for about 8 billion dollars. It makes thermal cameras and sensors for defence, security, industrial inspection, automotive and handheld consumer uses, plus unmanned systems and detection equipment. Customers are militaries, governments, industrial users and consumers via FLIR ONE and Lorex. Based in Wilsonville, Oregon, and widely known in thermal imaging, including use in motorsport inspection, though not a mass-market consumer name.

Typrotech is a Shanghai-based Chinese Internet of Things and physical security technology company, tagged by Crunchbase as IoT and physical security. Customers are industrial shippers, passengers and the state. Founded in 2003, it employs more than 700,000 people, with revenue of several trillion roubles, and is wholly owned by the Russian government. Highly visible consumer and industrial brand in Russia, but subject to sanctions since 2022.

Emaar MGF Land was an Indian real estate developer formed as a joint venture between Dubai's Emaar Properties and India's MGF Developments in 2005, building residential, commercial and retail projects such as Gurgaon's Palm Drive, Palm Gardens, and malls in Delhi NCR and other cities. Customers are builders, construction firms, contractors, car makers and industries, in about 75 countries, with revenue near 46 billion euros and over 160,000 staff. Divarian Propiedad was a Spanish real estate joint venture formed in 2014 by Blackstone and Banco Popular (Popular's bad-asset arm) around Madrid, in which Blackstone bought the majority of a portfolio of Spanish commercial property loans and real estate, run by Divarian Propiedad which held and managed the assets for later sale. Customers are Chinese home buyers, sellers and renters, and revenue comes from brokerage commissions, home renovation and rental services. Founded in 2001 and based in Beijing, KE Holdings is listed on the NYSE (BEKE) and Hong Kong. Widely recognised across Chinese cities, and a large consumer-facing brand.

Lucid Energy Group is a Dallas-based US midstream oil and gas company that built gathering, processing and compression infrastructure in the Permian Basin, including the Red Hills gas processing complex in the Delaware Basin in New Mexico and Texas, with capacity of several hundred million cubic feet a day. Customers are oil and gas producers who pay fees for handling gas. It was backed by Energy Capital Partners and Riverstone and was sold to Targa Resources in 2022 for about 3.5 billion dollars. No consumer profile.

Workspace Property Trust was a US office and flex real estate company based in Horsham, Pennsylvania, that owned and managed office properties and business parks, mainly in the eastern US. Crunchbase tags it only as real estate. I cannot confirm the details of its ownership or current status. It was a B2B landlord serving corporate tenants, with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DaDa is a Chinese online English education company that runs live one-to-one online English classes for children, taught by foreign teachers, through the DaDa app. Revenue comes from course packages paid by parents. Based in Shanghai, it listed on Nasdaq (DAO) in 2020 and has since reworked its business after Chinese regulation hit the after-school tutoring sector in 2021. Moderate awareness among Chinese parents, limited global recognition, and little relevance to a sponsor outside China.

Helios Towers is a pan-African telecom infrastructure company, headquartered in London, that builds, owns and operates mobile phone towers and leases space on them to mobile network operators such as Vodacom, Airtel and Orange across Tanzania, DRC, Ghana, South Africa, Congo-Brazzaville, Senegal, Malawi, Madagascar and Oman. It has around 14,000 towers and is listed on the London Stock Exchange (HTWS). B2B infrastructure provider with little consumer awareness, although it has an Africa-wide brand profile among telcos and investors.

VIPKid was a Chinese online education company that connected North American teachers with Chinese children aged about 4 to 12 for live one-to-one English lessons, delivered through its app and platform. Parents paid for course packages, and it grew to several hundred thousand students before China's 2021 crackdown on after-school tutoring cut its business sharply and it shifted toward other products and overseas expansion. Based in Beijing and backed by Tencent, Sequoia China and others at a valuation once above 3 billion dollars, and never listed. Well-known with Chinese parents but not a global consumer brand.

Avenue Bellevue is a two-tower mixed-use real estate development in downtown Bellevue, Washington, with office, residential and retail space on a prime site near the city's transit and tech employers. It is a single property project rather than an operating brand, built by a private development group. Tenants and residents are the audience, and revenue would come from leases and condo or rental income. Little consumer brand profile and no sponsorship track record. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

BGL Group is a UK financial services and insurance distribution business that runs price comparison websites and digital brands, including Compare the Market (the UK's best-known price comparison site, famous for its Meerkat Aleksandr Orlov campaign), Budget Insurance, Dial Direct and BISL for dealer insurance. Revenue comes from commission on insurance, energy and finance referrals. Based in Peterborough and owned by CVC Capital Partners since 2018. Very high consumer brand visibility in the UK, with significant TV advertising and sports sponsorship experience, which makes it a familiar sponsor profile.

BIDV (Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam) is one of Vietnam's largest state-controlled commercial banks, offering retail, corporate and investment banking, with a large branch network across the country, a presence in Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar and Russia, and a stake in BIDV Insurance and securities units. Founded in 1957, it is listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (BID), with the State Bank of Vietnam as majority owner and Korea's KEB Hana Bank a strategic shareholder. Large consumer-facing banking brand in Vietnam with sports and community sponsorship activity.

Hamilton Insurance Group is a Bermuda-based specialty insurance and reinsurance group that writes insurance through Hamilton Global Specialty and Lloyd's Syndicate 4000, plus reinsurance via Hamilton Re and an investment arm managed by Hamilton Investment Management. Customers are businesses and insurers, and revenue comes from premiums and investment returns. Founded in 2013 and listed on the NYSE (HG) since its 2023 IPO, with offices in Bermuda, London, Dublin and the US. B2B insurance brand known in specialty markets, with little consumer awareness.

IRB Infrastructure Developers is an Indian highway construction and toll road operator, building and running roads on build-operate-transfer and toll-operate-transfer models, including a number of national highways such as the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, and it has infrastructure investment trusts. Customers are government bodies, and it earns toll and construction revenue. Based in Mumbai and listed on NSE and BSE (IRB), it is among the larger Indian road developers. B2B infrastructure brand, which has some public visibility through toll plazas, but little consumer marketing.

Retail Properties of America was a US real estate investment trust that owned and managed shopping centres, mostly grocery-anchored and open-air centres in the US, in Sunbelt and other markets. Tenants included grocers, restaurants and retailers, and revenue came from rents. It was listed on the NYSE (RPAI) and was merged into Kite Realty Group in 2021. B2B landlord with no consumer-facing brand and no longer an independent company.

Security Bank is one of the Philippines' leading universal banks, offering consumer, corporate and treasury services, including savings and credit cards, loans, wealth management and a digital bank, with a branch network across the Philippines. Founded in 1951, it is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (SECB) and is majority owned by the Philippines' Sy-family and Securities Investment Corp. Consumer-facing banking brand with moderate recognition in the country, and local sponsorship in sports and events.

Sweet Oak Parent LLC is a Delaware limited liability company headquartered in Roswell, Georgia. The name is a holding company structure, and the Crunchbase description gives no operating details. I cannot identify the underlying business, its customers or its brand with confidence. It reports sizeable funding, which suggests a financing or private equity holding vehicle. No known consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Ucommune is a Chinese flexible workspace operator that offers co-working offices, private offices, event space and community services for small and medium businesses, start-ups and freelancers in Beijing and other cities, plus managed workspaces for corporates. Revenue comes from membership and rental fees. Founded in 2015 as Ucommune (UWork), it listed on Nasdaq (UK) via a SPAC merger in 2022, but it has downsized with the post-pandemic downturn. Known in Chinese co-working circles, and it has shifted toward offering workspace services.

Unacademy is an Indian online learning platform which offers live and recorded classes for competitive exam preparation, such as UPSC civil services, JEE, NEET and banking tests, taught by educators who build their followings on the app. Students pay subscriptions, and it has also had offline centres and test-prep acquisitions (Graphy and others). Founded in 2015 in Bengaluru, backed by General Atlantic, SoftBank and Temasek, valued at around 3.4 billion dollars in 2021, but has been cutting costs since 2022. Strongly recognised by Indian exam aspirants and has run cricket and entertainment advertising.

Godrej Garden City is a large integrated township in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, developed by Godrej Properties, one of India's leading listed real estate developers, offering apartments, villas and plots on a big site with parks and schools. It is a development rather than a company, and customers are homebuyers. Godrej Properties is part of the Godrej Group and is listed on NSE and BSE (GODREJPROP), with projects across Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru and the NCR. Godrej is a very well-known Indian consumer and property brand.

Jinke (Jinke Property Group) is a Chinese real estate developer based in Chongqing that builds residential and commercial properties across western China and many other cities, under the Jinke brand with services such as property management. It sells apartments to home buyers and earns development revenue. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (000656), it has faced heavy debt problems since 2021 and defaulted on bonds, with restructuring efforts underway. Regional recognition in China but a weak financial position, so not an attractive sponsor prospect.

LHG Mining (Lhg Mineracao) is a Brazilian iron ore mining company based in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, operating in the Corumba area, producing iron ore lump and fines sold to steelmakers, with some exports. It is a private mining business owned by a Brazilian family group, with significant debt financing. B2B commodity producer with no consumer profile, no known sponsorship activity and little reason to buy F1 exposure. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Spark Education Group (Spark Education) is a global online education company, which provides online language and learning programs such as English tutoring and school subject classes through a digital platform, tagged by Crunchbase as EBooks, EdTech and education. It serves consumers and learners in Asia and other markets and reports around 593 million dollars of funding, which suggests a substantial private business. I cannot confirm product names or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Tricon Residential is a Toronto-based owner and operator of single-family rental homes and multifamily apartments in the US Sunbelt and Canada, with tens of thousands of homes across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Georgia and Toronto. Customers are renters, and revenue comes from rents. Founded in 1988 as Tricon Capital, it was listed on the TSX and NYSE (TCN) and was taken private by Blackstone in 2024 in a deal of about 3.5 billion dollars. Little consumer profile outside rental housing, so brand visibility is modest.

African Metallic Resources is a Liberia-based mining and resources company focused on mineral development. Crunchbase gives little detail beyond that and shows funding of about 500 million dollars. I cannot confirm what metals or projects it holds, its ownership, or whether it operates producing assets. It would be a B2B commodity business, with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

FG Gold is a privately held gold exploration and mining company based in Sierra Leone, tagged by Crunchbase as mining. It is associated with a gold project in the country, though I cannot confirm the details or current ownership. It is a B2B commodity business with essentially no public brand awareness, and the funding figure shown is large relative to its profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Koton is a Turkish fashion retailer selling affordable ready-to-wear clothing for women, men and children, with a few hundred stores in Turkey and abroad, plus an online store, in markets such as Europe, Russia and the Middle East. Customers are mass-market fashion shoppers, and revenue comes from retail sales of its own-brand collections. Founded in 1988 and based in Istanbul, it listed on Borsa Istanbul (KTN) in 2024. A well-known fashion brand in Turkey, with visible advertising and sports links in the Turkish market.

Kr Space (36Kr Space) is a Chinese co-working space operator in Beijing set up by the technology media group 36Kr, offering shared and private offices, start-up incubation, events and community services for tech start-ups, with locations across Chinese cities. Revenue comes from rent and service fees, and it operated as one of China's earlier large co-working brands. Known in Chinese start-up circles through its media parent, and it has limited recognition abroad. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

PayFit is a French software company that automates payroll, HR and payslip management for small and medium businesses through a cloud platform, with features covering time-off, expenses and legal compliance. Customers are around 20,000 companies in France, the UK, Germany and Spain, who pay monthly subscriptions. Founded in 2016 in Paris, it is VC-backed (Meridiam, Accel, Eurazeo and Bpifrance) and valued above 2 billion dollars in 2021. B2B brand with significant awareness among French HR and finance teams, and it has run advertising campaigns in France.

Pebl is a US company in Palo Alto, California, described by Crunchbase as offering a global employment solution, covering hiring and employing workers across countries. It reports roughly 500 million dollars of funding, though I cannot reliably identify this specific company or its ownership. Likely a B2B HR technology and employment services business with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Qarmet, formerly ArcelorMittal Temirtau, is Kazakhstan's largest steel and coal producer, making slabs, hot-rolled and cold-rolled steel, rebar and wire from its integrated steel plant in Temirtau, and mining coal and iron ore in the Karaganda region. It was acquired in 2023 by Kazakh businessman Kenes Rakishev's group, buying ArcelorMittal's Kazakh assets for several billion dollars. Customers are construction, automotive and manufacturing firms across Central Asia, Russia and beyond. Large B2B industrial employer with high domestic profile but little consumer marketing.

Mecachrome is a French precision engineering and manufacturing group that makes engine components, aerostructures and machined parts for aerospace, motorsport and automotive customers. It built race engines, most famously the Mecachrome-badged Formula 1 engines of the late 1990s (Renault-derived units), and supplied components for Formula 1, MotoGP and Le Mans programmes, plus aerospace parts for Airbus and Safran. It is privately owned and a B2B supplier with a long motorsport heritage but a low public profile.

Bedrock Real Estate Services is a Detroit-based US property company founded by Dan Gilbert, which develops, owns, leases and manages commercial and residential real estate, with a large portfolio of downtown Detroit buildings, and also in Cleveland and Cincinnati, including the Hudson's Site tower. Customers are tenants, residents and retail businesses. It is privately held and co-founded with Quicken Loans founder Gilbert's family. Well known in Detroit and Michigan, with community profile, but a niche brand elsewhere.

Halter is a New Zealand agtech company that makes a solar-powered smart collar for cattle, which lets farmers move, steer and monitor herds from a phone app using sound and vibration cues instead of fences. Customers are dairy and beef farmers in New Zealand, Australia and the US, who pay hardware and subscription fees. Founded in 2016 by Craig Piggott and based in Auckland, it is venture-backed (Bond, Blackbird and others) and has been valued at around 1 billion dollars. Well known among farmers, with modest general awareness.

Paper is a Canadian education technology company offering on-demand tutoring, which provides students with unlimited online help from tutors for homework and writing, sold primarily to school districts and state education departments, including through partnerships in Texas and elsewhere in the US. Revenue comes from district and public sector contracts. Founded in Montreal in 2014, it is venture-backed by firms like Sorenson and Mesa. B2B and public sector brand, known among US school administrators, with little general consumer awareness.

Acumen Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing sabirnetug (ACU193), an antibody that targets toxic soluble amyloid-beta oligomers in early Alzheimer's disease. It has no approved products and funds trials via equity raising. Founded in 2021 as a spin-out from work at Northwestern University and Merck, it listed on Nasdaq (ABOS) in 2021. Scientific audience of investors and clinicians, with no consumer brand awareness.

Altimmune is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing pemvidutide, a peptide for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and obesity, plus other candidates such as AMP-2 and HepTcell. It has no approved products and funds trials through equity, and is listed on Nasdaq (ALT). Founded in 1997, it has pivoted after earlier vaccine work. Pre-revenue, small and aimed at investors and clinicians, with no consumer brand awareness.

Alzheon is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing valiltramiprosate (ALZ-801), an oral small-molecule drug for early Alzheimer's disease in people with two copies of the APOE4 gene, plus other compounds targeting neurodegeneration. It has no approved products, and runs pivotal trials, financed by private investors. Founded in 2013 and based near Boston. Known to the scientific and investor community, with no consumer brand awareness and little sponsorship relevance.

Anteris Technologies is a structural heart company that develops the DurAVR transcatheter aortic valve, a single-piece biomimetic heart valve made with its ADAPT tissue technology, for patients with aortic stenosis, and a DurAVR trial programme. It was originally the Australian-listed Admedus, and was redomiciled to the US and listed on Nasdaq (AVR) in 2024, while keeping an ASX presence. Customers are cardiologists and hospitals. Small, pre-commercial and with no consumer awareness.

Apnimed is a US clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing oral drugs for obstructive sleep apnea, led by AD109, a combination of aroxybutynin and atomoxetine designed to improve airway muscle control during sleep. It has no approved product yet and finances trials through venture capital. Founded in 2016 by MIT and Harvard researchers, backed by Gilde and others, with a growing portfolio. Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness, though sleep health is a consumer topic.

Armata Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing bacteriophage (phage) therapies, natural viruses that kill bacteria, to treat antibiotic-resistant infections such as Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia and Pseudomonas lung infections in cystic fibrosis. It has no approved products and is funded by equity and by Innoviva as a major shareholder. Founded as AmpliPhi, it merged with Armata in 2019 and is listed on NYSE American (ARMP). Scientific brand with no consumer awareness.

AusperBio is a Chinese biotechnology company focused on RNA interference (siRNA) drugs for chronic hepatitis B and other liver diseases. It was reported to have been acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2023 and was previously based in Hangzhou, with US operations. Revenue was limited and mostly came from financing. It is a science-led pharma business with no consumer brand awareness and no sponsorship activity, so it is not a sponsor prospect.

Basilea Pharmaceutica is a Swiss commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company that focuses on anti-infectives, with products such as Cresemba (isavuconazole) for severe fungal infections, licensed to Pfizer and Astellas, and Zevtera (ceftobiprole) for bacterial infections, plus a pipeline of antifungal and antibacterial candidates. Customers are hospitals and licensing partners, and revenue is from royalties, milestone payments and product sales. Founded in 2000 as a spin-out of Roche and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (BSLN). Well respected in infectious disease circles, but no consumer brand awareness.

Beacon Therapeutics is a UK-based biotechnology company developing gene therapies for inherited retinal diseases, led by laruparetigene zovaparvovec (AGTC-501) for X-linked retinitis pigmentosa, plus candidates for dry age-related macular degeneration. It was set up in 2022 with Syncona backing after acquiring AGTC's assets from Applied Genetic Technologies. No approved products yet, and it relies on venture funding. Science-driven, with no consumer awareness, and limited sponsorship relevance.

Bright Minds Biosciences is a Canadian-listed biotechnology company with US ties that develops serotonin-targeting drugs, derived from psychedelic compounds but designed without the hallucinogenic effect, for epilepsy and neuropsychiatric conditions, with lead candidate BMB-101. It is pre-revenue, listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange and Nasdaq (DRUG), and funds its programmes through equity raises. It is an early-stage science business known to investors and specialists, with no consumer brand awareness and little sponsorship relevance.

Cepton is a US developer of lidar sensors for automotive and smart infrastructure, using its proprietary Micro Motion Technology design for advanced driver assistance systems, with a major production programme with Japan's Koito for vehicles, and industrial and traffic uses. Customers are carmakers, lighting suppliers and infrastructure firms. It listed on Nasdaq (CPTN) via a 2022 SPAC merger and was acquired by Koito Manufacturing in 2025. B2B technology brand known in the lidar sector, with no consumer awareness.

CityNet Telecommunications was a US provider of broadband infrastructure that built fibre networks in cities, using the sewer system and utility rights of way to bring fibre to buildings and wireless towers, serving carriers and enterprises in Maryland and other states. Customers were wholesale telecom carriers and businesses. It was venture-funded, and later acquired within the telecom infrastructure sector. B2B infrastructure with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Controladora Comercial Mexicana was a Mexican retail group, one of the country's largest supermarket and department store operators, with the Comercial Mexicana, Mega, Bodega Comercial Mexicana, Sumesa and City Market banners, and restaurants (California). Customers were mass-market Mexican shoppers. It was sold to the Soriana group in 2015, after a derivatives crisis in 2008, and the brands were absorbed or rebranded. Once a household name in Mexico, no longer operating independently.

Crystalys Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for gout and related conditions, with a lead candidate for patients whose uric acid is not controlled by existing drugs. It was founded to advance a drug acquired from another company and financed by venture investors. Pre-revenue and small, with no consumer brand awareness and no sponsorship track record. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DaAn Gene is a Chinese molecular diagnostics company based in Guangzhou, known for PCR test kits for infectious diseases, including hepatitis B and C and HPV, and for COVID-19 nucleic acid tests, plus genetic testing, prenatal screening and diagnostic equipment. Customers are hospitals, labs and public health bodies in China. Founded in 1988 and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002030), it is linked to Sun Yat-sen University. B2B healthcare brand, widely used within China's medical system, with little consumer awareness.

DarioHealth is a US-Israeli digital health company that sells a mobile-app platform and connected devices for managing chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, weight and musculoskeletal pain, including Dario glucose meters, coaching and AI-driven programmes. Customers are employers, health plans and consumers. Founded in 2011 and listed on Nasdaq (DRIO), it has acquired companies such as Twill and Upright. Moderate awareness among digital health buyers, with modest consumer recognition.

Elicio Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing lymph-node-targeted cancer vaccines using its Amphiphile (AMP) technology, led by ELI-002 for pancreatic cancer and other KRAS-mutated tumours. It has no approved products and funds trials through equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (ELTX) after merging with Angion Biomedica in 2023. Science-led business known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer brand awareness and no sponsorship track record.

Enable Injections is a US medical device company that develops and makes the enFuse wearable on-body injector, which delivers large-volume drugs subcutaneously, so patients can self-administer biologic therapies at home. Customers are pharmaceutical companies, who partner and pay for development and supply, with devices produced in Cincinnati, Ohio. Privately held and venture-backed. B2B healthcare technology with no consumer brand awareness.

Forte Biosciences is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing FB102, an antibody that targets CD122 for autoimmune diseases such as celiac disease, vitiligo and alopecia areata, after earlier work on topical products. It has no approved products and funds trials through equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (FBRX). Small science-led business known only to investors and specialists, with no consumer brand awareness and no sponsorship relevance.

Full-Life Technologies is a Belgian-headquartered radiopharmaceutical company that develops radiotherapies and diagnostics for cancer using radioactive isotopes attached to targeting molecules, with R&D bases in Belgium, Germany, China and the US. It has no approved products and is financed by venture capital. Founded in 2018, it has partnerships and licensing with other drug makers. Scientific audience of investors and clinicians, with no consumer awareness.

Hailo is an Israeli semiconductor company that designs AI processors for edge devices, such as the Hailo-8 and Hailo-10 chips used in cameras, cars, industrial robots and smart cities for deep-learning inference at low power. Customers are device makers and automotive suppliers. Founded in 2017 in Tel Aviv and backed by Zeev Ventures, Poalim, Samsung and others, with a valuation above 1 billion dollars. B2B chip supplier with little consumer awareness.

Heidelberg Pharma is a German biopharmaceutical company that develops antibody-drug conjugates for cancer using its proprietary Antibody Targeted Amanitin Conjugate (ATAC) technology, with lead candidate HDP-101 for multiple myeloma, and it earns revenue from collaborations and research services. Controlled by Dietmar Hopp's dievini Hopp BioTech holding and listed in Frankfurt (HPHA). Based in Ladenburg, with a long research heritage in Germany. Science-focused business with no consumer awareness.

InfraBuild is an Australian steel manufacturer and distributor, formed from the former Liberty OneSteel and part of Sanjeev Gupta's GFG Alliance. It produces long steel products including rebar, wire, rail, pipe and structural steel, and operates recycling and steel distribution, with Whyalla-linked operations. Customers are construction, mining, rail and infrastructure firms. Operates sites throughout Australia, with several thousand staff, and a strong B2B profile in Australian building trades, though not a consumer brand.

Innate Pharma is a French biotechnology company developing antibody therapies for cancer, using the immune system's natural killer cells, including lacutamab for T-cell lymphoma and ANKET engagers, and it earns revenue from partnerships with AstraZeneca and Sanofi. Based in Marseille, founded in 1999 and listed on Euronext Paris and Nasdaq (IPH). Science-focused business known to investors and clinicians, with no consumer brand awareness.

Korro Bio is a US biotechnology company developing RNA editing medicines, using ADAR enzymes to correct genetic errors in RNA, with candidates for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and other diseases, and partnership with Novo Nordisk. It has no approved products and was formed in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Listed on Nasdaq (KRRO) after merging with Frequency Therapeutics in 2023. Science-driven with no consumer brand awareness.

Leyden Labs is a Dutch biotechnology company, spun out of Leiden, developing intranasal antibody and antiviral treatments to prevent respiratory infections such as influenza and RSV, using a nasal spray designed to protect against many virus strains. It has no approved products and was founded in 2020 by Pfizer and Janssen-linked scientists, backed by large private investors. Science-led with no current consumer brand, though a product could eventually reach consumers.

Mirxes is a Singapore-based molecular diagnostics company that develops blood tests based on microRNA biomarkers for early cancer detection, notably GASTROClear for gastric cancer, which has been approved in China, plus lung and liver cancer screening tests. Customers are hospitals and health screening providers, mostly in China and Southeast Asia. Founded in 2008 as a spin-out of Singapore research institutions. Science-driven healthcare brand with limited consumer awareness, though cancer screening is a consumer-facing topic in Asia.

Chengdu New Radiomedicine Technology is a Chinese biotechnology company developing radiopharmaceuticals, drugs that use radioactive isotopes to diagnose and treat cancer. Crunchbase notes funding of around 2.3 billion yuan. I do not have reliable details of its pipeline, owners or products. A B2B healthcare business with no consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Ninjacart is an Indian business-to-business fresh produce supply chain platform which buys fruit and vegetables directly from farmers and delivers them to retailers, restaurants and kirana stores in cities such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Mumbai. It earns revenue from the margin on produce and logistics, and uses data and technology to cut waste. Founded in 2015 in Bengaluru, backed by Walmart, Tiger Global and Flipkart. A B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though recognised in the Indian agritech sector.
