NoBroker is an Indian real estate platform connecting property owners with tenants and buyers directly, without brokers, through its app and website, and offering services such as rental agreements, packers and movers, home interiors, home loans and tenant verification. It earns revenue from subscription and service fees, with millions of users in cities such as Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad. Founded in 2014 and backed by General Atlantic and Tiger Global, it became a unicorn in 2021. Recognised among Indian urban renters, with heavy digital advertising.

Oishii is a US vertical farming company that grows premium strawberries, including its Omakase Berry, in indoor vertical farms in New Jersey using pollination by bees in controlled environments. Customers are consumers and high-end retailers like Whole Foods, restaurants and grocery stores, sold under the Oishii brand. Founded in 2016 in Japan and later based in New Jersey, it is backed by Wicklow and others. A niche premium consumer food brand with limited broad awareness.

OnKure Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing targeted cancer drugs, led by OKI-219, a mutant-selective PI3K alpha inhibitor for breast cancer and other solid tumours. It has no approved products and funds trials through equity raises. Based in Boulder, Colorado, and listed on Nasdaq (OKUR) after merging with Reneo Pharmaceuticals in 2024. Science-led business known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship relevance.

Ovid Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing medicines for rare neurological disorders, including epilepsy, with candidates such as OV329 and OV350, after earning royalties from Takeda on soticlestat. It has no approved products and funds programmes through equity and royalty deals. Founded in 2014 and listed on Nasdaq (OVID). Scientific and investor audience, with no consumer brand awareness.

Paratek Pharmaceuticals is a US commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company that markets Nuzyra (omadacycline), an antibiotic for community-acquired pneumonia and skin infections, and Xerava-linked products, selling to hospitals, plus government contracts for anthrax and biodefence uses. It has been small, with revenue of around 150 to 200 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (PRTK), it was taken private in 2023 by Gurnet Point Capital and Novo Holdings for about 462 million dollars. Known to infectious disease clinicians, with no consumer awareness.

Precision BioSciences is a US clinical-stage gene editing company built on its proprietary ARCUS genome editing platform, a nuclease derived from a natural meganuclease, with candidates for chronic hepatitis B (PBGENE-HBV) and for muscle disease, plus partnerships with Novartis and Prevail (Lilly). It has no approved products and funds programmes through equity and collaborations. Founded in 2006 and listed on Nasdaq (DTIL). Scientific brand with no consumer awareness.

Quince Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing eDSP, an autologous red blood cell delivery of dexamethasone for ataxia telangiectasia, a rare neurological disease, after acquiring EryDel in 2023. The company was previously Cortexyme, which pursued Alzheimer's therapies before pivoting. It has no approved products, and is listed on Nasdaq (QNCX). Known to investors and rare-disease specialists, with no consumer brand awareness.

Rein Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, formerly Aeolus Pharmaceuticals, developing LTI-03, an inhaled peptide treatment for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and other fibrotic lung diseases. It has no approved products and is financed by equity, and is listed on Nasdaq (RNTX) following its merger with Aeolus in 2024. Based in Austin, Texas. Small and known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Retail Opportunity Investments Corp. (ROIC) is a US real estate investment trust that owns and manages grocery-anchored shopping centres on the West Coast, in California, Oregon and Washington, in dense suburban markets. Tenants include supermarkets, pharmacies and service retailers, and revenue comes from rents. Listed on Nasdaq (ROIC), with a portfolio of dozens of properties. B2B landlord with no consumer brand relevance, and not a typical sponsor.

Seaport Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing neuropsychiatric medicines, using its proprietary Glyph platform to improve the oral delivery of drugs for depression, anxiety and related disorders, including SPT-300 (a prodrug of allopregnanolone). It has no approved products and was founded in 2022 with backing from Flagship-linked investors and venture funds, including Third Rock. Science-focused business with no consumer brand awareness yet.

Sonendo is a US medical device company that makes the GentleWave System for root canal treatment, which uses fluid dynamics to clean teeth without removing as much tooth structure. Customers are dentists and endodontists, who buy the system and pay per procedure for consumables. Listed on the NYSE (SONX) in 2021, it later ran into financial difficulty. Known among dental professionals, with no direct consumer awareness, and a small commercial base.

Souffle Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company developing RNA-based medicines with a delivery approach designed to target cancer cells with potent and precise therapies. It is privately held and venture-funded and has no approved products. I know little beyond its stated focus. Science-driven, with no consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Spruce Biosciences is a US biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for rare endocrine disorders, with tildacerfont for classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (which failed in trials) and later TA-ERT for the rare lysosomal disease Sanfilippo syndrome (MPS IIIB), licensed from Allievex. It has no approved products and is listed on Nasdaq (SPRB). Based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Known to rare-disease specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Terremoto Biosciences is a US biotechnology company, based in the San Francisco Bay Area and tagged simply as biotechnology. It is a private, venture-backed start-up founded in 2021 with a chemoproteomics approach to discover drugs that bind proteins not usually targeted. I cannot confirm more. Early stage with no consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Tonix Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage and early commercial pharmaceutical company. It markets Tonmya (a sublingual cyclobenzaprine) for fibromyalgia, approved in 2025, owns the Zembrace and Tosymra migraine products, and has vaccine and immunology candidates. Customers are prescribers and patients in the US. Listed on Nasdaq (TNXP), with a history of heavy dilution. Known to investors, with modest public awareness through its fibromyalgia marketing.

Weiyuan Synthetic Biotechnology is a Chinese synthetic biology company in Beijing which uses engineered microorganisms to make products such as food ingredients and bio-based materials. Crunchbase tags it as biotechnology and food, with a large yuan funding total of about 2.5 billion yuan. I cannot confirm its product lines or ownership. B2B ingredient supplier with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Werewolf Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing conditionally activated cytokine immunotherapies for cancer, using its INDUKINE platform, with candidates such as WTX-124 (IL-2) and WTX-330 (IL-12). It has no approved products and funds trials through equity and a collaboration with Jazz Pharmaceuticals. Listed on Nasdaq (HOWL). Science-focused business known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

West Fraser Timber is a Canadian forest products company and one of the world's largest lumber producers, making lumber, plywood, oriented strand board (OSB), medium-density fibreboard and pulp, with mills in western Canada, the US South and Europe (after buying Norbord in 2021). Customers are builders and wholesale distributors. Revenue is in the billions of dollars and it has more than 10,000 staff. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (WFG), founded in 1955 in British Columbia. A B2B commodity producer with little consumer awareness.

Windward Bio is a Swiss-headquartered biotechnology company developing a long-acting antibody against TSLP for asthma and other inflammatory diseases, licensed from Chinese drug maker Hengrui. It was launched in 2024 with large venture funding from specialist biotech investors and has no approved products. Customers will be physicians and patients in respiratory medicine in future. Science-driven company with no consumer brand awareness and no sponsorship track record.

Xilio Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing masked, tumour-activated immunotherapies, including cytokines and T-cell engagers, designed to work in the tumour but not in healthy tissue, with candidates such as vilastobart (anti-CTLA-4) and efarindodekin alfa (IL-12). It has no approved products and works with partners such as AbbVie and Gilead. Listed on Nasdaq (XLO). Known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Zura Bio is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing antibodies for immune and inflammatory diseases, including tibulizumab (targeting BAFF and IL-17), torudokimab (IL-33) and crebankitug, for conditions like systemic sclerosis and hidradenitis suppurativa. It has no approved products and listed on Nasdaq (ZURA) via a SPAC merger in 2023. Science-focused business known to investors and immunology specialists, with no consumer brand awareness and no sponsorship relevance.

Alector is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing antibody therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, targeting immune cells in the brain, with programmes in frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer's, and partnerships with AbbVie and GSK. It has no approved products and funds trials through partnerships and equity. Founded in 2013 and listed on Nasdaq (ALEC). Science-driven, known to neurology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Apollomics is a clinical-stage oncology company with US and China operations developing targeted cancer drugs, including vebreltinib (a MET inhibitor) for lung cancer and other tumours, plus other candidates. It has no approved products in the West. Listed on Nasdaq (APLM) after a 2023 SPAC merger. Science-led business with no consumer awareness, and finances that depend on capital raising, so it is not a realistic sponsorship prospect.

AVITA Medical is a regenerative medicine company that sells the RECELL System, a device that makes a spray of a patient's own skin cells for treating burns, wounds and skin pigmentation loss, plus Cohealyx and PermeaDerm products. Customers are burn centres, hospitals and surgeons, and revenue comes from device and consumable sales in the US. Originally an Australian company, now US-headquartered, it is listed on Nasdaq (RCEL) and the ASX. Known to surgeons, with no general consumer awareness.

Beren Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company developing treatments for rare and genetic diseases, with a focus on conditions affecting children. It is private and venture-backed, and I cannot confirm its pipeline. No approved products, no consumer awareness, and no sponsorship track record. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

BlackSoil is an Indian non-bank lender and advisory firm based in Mumbai, offering structured credit and venture debt to growing businesses, with a background in agriculture and rural finance, and supporting investors. It reports roughly 310 million dollars of funding. Revenue comes from interest and fees. Privately held with little consumer awareness, known mainly to small and mid-size Indian businesses and financial investors. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

BTI Telecom was a US integrated communications provider based in Raleigh, North Carolina, offering local and long-distance voice, data and internet services to small and mid-size businesses in the Southeast, along with outsourced services. It was a competitive local exchange carrier in the 1990s and 2000s, funded by large debt issues, and eventually went through restructuring and was acquired by a larger telecom provider. No consumer profile and no longer operating independently. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cambrian Biopharma is a US biotechnology company, founded by James Peyer, that builds a portfolio of drug candidates targeting the biology of ageing, intending to extend healthy lifespan. It works through a distributed model of subsidiary companies, each focused on specific diseases. It has no approved products. Venture-funded and little known to the public, but notable among longevity investors, with no consumer awareness or sponsorship track record.

CapitaLand Ascott Trust is a Singapore-listed real estate investment trust and one of the largest lodging trusts globally, owning serviced residences, rental housing and hotels operated under brands such as Ascott, Citadines, Somerset and lyf, and the Quest and Oakwood names, across Asia Pacific, Europe and the US. Revenue comes from rents and management fees. Sponsored by CapitaLand Investment and listed on the SGX (HMN). B2B ownership vehicle, while the operating brands are well known to business travellers.

Cellanome is a US biotechnology instrument start-up developing a platform that can analyse the biology of single living cells and their interactions at scale, for use in genomics, drug discovery and cell therapy research. It was launched in 2024 with large venture funding and a founding team including Stanford and Illumina-linked scientists. Customers will be research labs and drug makers. Early stage with no consumer awareness.

CenterPoint Broadband Technologies is a US telecommunications business that developed high-capacity broadband access technology and services for residential customers, as a venture-funded business in Oak Brook, Illinois, backed by large energy utilities. It sought to deliver multi-service fibre-based networks, but I cannot confirm whether it continued operations. No consumer profile today. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cerus is a US biomedical products company that sells the INTERCEPT Blood System, which treats donated platelets and plasma with pathogen-reduction technology to prevent transfusion-transmitted infections. Customers are blood centres and hospitals in the US, Europe and elsewhere, and revenue is around 150 to 200 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (CERS) and headquartered in Concord, California. Known to transfusion medicine specialists, with no general consumer awareness.

Circle Pharma is a US biotechnology company developing macrocycle drugs, a class of cyclic peptide-like molecules, aimed at cancer targets that are hard to reach, notably cell-cycle (cyclin) inhibitors, with candidate CID-078. It is private and venture backed, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It has no approved products and no consumer awareness, and is known only to investors and oncology specialists, so it has little sponsorship relevance.

Cognito Therapeutics is a US medical device company developing the Spectris device, a non-invasive headset that delivers 40Hz sensory stimulation (light and sound) to try to treat Alzheimer's disease by driving brain gamma oscillations, based on MIT research. It is running a pivotal clinical trial and has no approved product. Privately held and venture backed. Known in neuroscience and investor circles, with no consumer awareness yet.

Corporate Office Properties Trust (COPT), now COPT Defense Properties, is a US real estate investment trust that owns and operates office and data centre properties, concentrated near US Defense and intelligence agency sites and installations, such as Fort Meade in Maryland. Tenants are government contractors and agencies, and revenue comes from rents. Based in Columbia, Maryland, and listed on the NYSE (CDP, formerly OFC). B2B landlord with no consumer brand.

CREATE Medicines is a US biotechnology company, formerly Myeloid Therapeutics, developing in vivo CAR therapies, using mRNA delivered to patients to program their own immune cells to fight cancer and autoimmune disease, without cell manufacturing outside the body. It is privately held and venture backed, with no approved products. Science-driven company known to biotech investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record.

Curis is a US biotechnology company that discovered Erivedge (vismodegib), a hedgehog pathway inhibitor for advanced basal cell carcinoma marketed by Roche/Genentech, from which it earns royalties, and now develops oncology candidates such as emavusertib for blood cancers. It has no major product revenue of its own. Listed on Nasdaq (CRIS) and based in Lexington, Massachusetts. Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

DFS Furniture is a UK furniture retailer, the country's largest sofa specialist, selling fabric and leather sofas, armchairs and sofa beds, mostly made to order, through about 100 showrooms and online. It also owns Sofology and the Sofa Workshop brands, along with the Dwell business, and has a strong TV advertising profile. Customers are mass-market and mid-market UK households. Founded in 1969 as Direct Furnishing Supplies, it is based in Doncaster and listed on the London Stock Exchange (DFS). A well-known consumer retailer in the UK with a history of heavy advertising and some sports and TV sponsorship.

Flare Therapeutics is a US biotechnology start-up developing precision medicines that target transcription factors, which control gene expression and have been hard to drug, with a first programme aimed at cancer. It was founded in 2019 with backing from Atlas Venture and others. Private and venture backed, with no approved products, no consumer awareness and no known sponsorship activity, so it is not a typical brand-sponsorship prospect.

GenSight Biologics is a French biotechnology company that develops gene therapy for retinal neurodegenerative diseases, led by Lumevoq (lenadogene nolparvovec) for Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, which it has distributed in France under an early access scheme. It also has optogenetic vision restoration research. Founded in 2012 and listed on Euronext Paris (SIGHT). Known to ophthalmology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

goFARM Australia is an Australian agricultural property developer and manager, based in Sydney, that invests in and operates farmland and agribusiness assets with institutional investors, such as horticulture and cropping properties. The name suggests a farm-focused investment vehicle, but I cannot confirm details. Revenue would come from farmland returns and development. B2B, private and with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Goodman Networks was a US telecom field services company that provided engineering, installation and maintenance for wireless carriers and cable operators, notably as a main contractor for AT&T, and handled network deployment and infrastructure services. It was based in Frisco, Texas, and heavily dependent on a few large customers. It filed for bankruptcy in 2017 and again later, and no longer operates as a major business. B2B contractor with no consumer profile.

Grande Communications was a US broadband provider headquartered in San Marcos, Texas, offering cable internet, TV and phone services to homes and businesses in Texas markets such as San Antonio, Austin and Corpus Christi, as an overbuilder competing with incumbents. It was acquired by private equity, later became part of the Radiate group and was combined into the Astound Broadband brand. It had local sponsorships in Texas. Today no standalone brand.

Grupo Lamosa is a Mexican building products group, based in Monterrey, that makes ceramic floor and wall tiles, bathroom fixtures, adhesives and mortars, and cement-based products under brands such as Lamosa, Interceramic (acquired 2018), Vitromex and Nexcer. It sells to builders, distributors and consumers, with operations in Mexico, the US and Latin America. Listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (LAMOSA). Known by Mexican consumers and in building trades.

JAPFA Group is an Indonesian-based agribusiness group, one of Southeast Asia's large integrated poultry and food companies, producing animal feed, day-old chicks, broilers, dairy products (Greenfields) and consumer food brands such as Real Good and So Good, along with aquaculture and beef feedlots. Customers are farmers, retailers and mass consumers, with operations in Indonesia, Vietnam, Myanmar and India. The Indonesian arm is listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (JPFA). Some consumer brands are well known in Indonesia.

JSW Cement is an Indian cement maker, part of the JSW Group, which produces Portland slag cement, Portland composite cement and ground granulated blast furnace slag using steel industry by-products, with several grinding and production plants in India. Customers are builders, infrastructure projects and retail buyers who see the JSW Cement and JSW brand. Based in Mumbai and listed in India (JSWCEMENT) in 2025. B2B-leaning building materials brand, supported by the strong JSW consumer-facing group name, which sponsors sports teams in India.

Kindbody is a US fertility and family-building clinic network, offering egg freezing, IVF, intrauterine insemination, fertility testing, gynaecology and employer fertility benefits, through clinics in cities such as New York, Los Angeles and Boston, plus mobile clinics. Customers are individuals and employers, and revenue comes from treatment fees and benefits contracts. Founded in 2018 by Gina Bartasi and venture backed, though it has had controversies and restructuring. Some consumer brand awareness among US women and benefits managers.

Life Biosciences is a US biotechnology company developing treatments for ageing-related diseases by partially reprogramming cells to restore their youthful function, with a lead programme (ER-100) for optic neuropathies such as glaucoma and NAION. Co-founded by David Sinclair of Harvard, it is private and venture backed with no approved products. Known in longevity circles, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record.

Lycia Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company developing lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs), a way of degrading extracellular and membrane proteins, with applications in cancer and autoimmune diseases. Founded on research from Stanford University by Carolyn Bertozzi's lab, it is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and was backed by Third Rock and others. It had collaborations with Lilly and Merck. No approved products and no consumer awareness.

Median Technologies is a French medical imaging software company, offering AI-based tools for cancer imaging in clinical trials (iBiopsy) and its iCRO imaging service for drug developers, plus a lung cancer screening software in development. Customers are pharmaceutical companies and clinical research organisations, and it earns revenue from imaging core lab services. Founded in 2002 and listed on Euronext Paris (ALMDT), located in Sophia Antipolis. B2B healthcare technology brand with no consumer awareness.

MedinCell is a French pharmaceutical company that develops long-acting injectable drugs using its BEPO polymer technology, which releases a drug steadily over weeks or months. Its lead products include an injectable risperidone for schizophrenia partnered with Teva (Uzedy) and programmes in contraception, malaria and pain. Revenue comes from licensing, royalties and partner payments. Based in Montpellier and listed on Euronext Paris (MEDCL). Known to pharma partners, with no consumer awareness.

Mighty Therapeutics is a US biopharmaceutical company in Newton, Massachusetts, tagged by Crunchbase as biopharma and biotechnology. It is private and venture backed, and I do not recognise its pipeline in enough detail to state it. No approved products and no consumer awareness are likely. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Nautilus Biotechnology is a US life sciences tools company developing a platform for measuring the whole proteome, the complete set of proteins in a sample, aimed at drug discovery and biomarker research customers. It has no commercial product yet and funds development with cash raised from its 2021 SPAC listing on Nasdaq (NAUT). Founded in 2016 by Sujal Patel, who earlier founded Isilon. Known in proteomics and investor circles, with no consumer awareness.

New Edge Networks is a US business telecom provider, based in Vancouver, Washington, that sold managed internet, private networking and voice services to multi-site businesses, using other carriers' networks and acting as a national aggregator. It was funded by venture capital and later combined with other providers. No consumer profile, and I cannot confirm its current status. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

ONWARD Medical is a Dutch-Swiss medical technology company that develops implantable and external spinal cord neurostimulation systems to restore movement in people with spinal cord injury, including the ARC-EX therapy cleared by the US FDA in 2024 and the ARC-IM and ARC-BCI platforms. Customers are rehabilitation clinics and patients. Listed on Euronext Brussels and Amsterdam (ONWD). Known in medtech and spinal injury communities, with inspiring human stories that could suit brand storytelling.

Palvella Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing QTORIN rapamycin, a topical formulation for rare skin diseases such as microcystic lymphatic malformations and pachyonychia congenita. It has no approved products and funds trials through equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (PVLA) after merging with Pieris Pharmaceuticals in 2024. Based in Wayne, Pennsylvania. Known to dermatology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Penn-Florida Companies is a US commercial real estate firm based in Boca Raton, Florida, that develops, owns and manages office, retail and mixed-use properties in the South Florida market, with a consulting component. It is privately held and has been active since the 1980s. B2B landlord and developer, known in local property circles, with no meaningful consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

PMV Pharmaceuticals is a US clinical-stage precision oncology company developing drugs that target the tumour suppressor protein p53, such as rezatapopt (PC14586) for cancers with the Y220C mutation. It has no approved products and funds trials through equity raises. Founded in 2013 and listed on Nasdaq (PMVP) in 2020, with offices in Princeton and Cambridge. Known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Prelude Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage oncology company developing targeted small-molecule drugs, including protein degraders and inhibitors such as an SMARCA2 degrader and a CDK9 inhibitor, and previously a JAK2 programme. It has no approved products and funds trials with equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (PRLD). Known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship relevance.

SCYNEXIS is a US biotechnology company that developed Brexafemme (ibrexafungerp), a first-in-class oral antifungal for vaginal yeast infections and a candidate for invasive fungal diseases, licensed to GSK in 2023 for a large upfront and milestone package. It earns revenue from licensing and limited product sales. Listed on Nasdaq (SCYX). Known to infectious disease specialists and investors, with minor consumer awareness.

Sera Prognostics is a US women's health diagnostics company that sells the PreTRM test, a blood test taken during pregnancy that estimates a woman's risk of preterm birth, based on proteomic biomarkers, and is developing further tests. Customers are obstetricians and health systems, with revenue from test sales and collaborations. Founded in 2008 and listed on Nasdaq (SERA). Known in maternal health circles, with modest consumer awareness.

Shoulder Innovations is a US medical device company that develops shoulder replacement implants and instruments, including its InSet glenoid components and a pre-planning approach, aimed at orthopaedic surgeons treating shoulder arthritis. Customers are surgeons, hospitals and surgery centres. Based in Holland, Michigan, it is venture backed and listed on the NYSE (SI) after a 2025 IPO. Known among orthopaedic specialists, with no consumer awareness.

Tenpoint Therapeutics is a UK-based biotechnology company focused on eye diseases, tagged by Crunchbase as biotechnology and health care. I recall it working on treatments for presbyopia, the age-related loss of near vision, but I cannot confirm its pipeline or ownership. It has no approved products yet and is venture backed. The condition is consumer-relevant, but there is no brand awareness at present. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

TM Group is a UK technology and services company in Swindon, which provides software and support to businesses such as telematics, customer experience and compliance tools for the automotive and other sectors. Crunchbase tags it as information technology. I cannot confirm detailed products or ownership. It likely has B2B customers in the UK with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Tower Vision is an Indian telecom tower company, based in Gurugram, that builds and operates passive mobile infrastructure, leasing space on towers to mobile network operators. Crunchbase tags it as mobile and telecommunications and shows sizeable funding of about 300 million dollars. Customers are telecom operators, so it is a pure B2B infrastructure provider with essentially no consumer brand. I cannot confirm tower counts or the owner. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

TPx Communications, formerly TelePacific, is a US managed services provider offering business internet, voice, SD-WAN, security and unified communications to multi-site businesses, with a network spanning the US. Customers are small and mid-size companies and franchise chains, and revenue comes from recurring service subscriptions. Based in Austin, Texas, and owned by private equity. B2B telecom brand known to IT buyers at multi-location businesses, with low general consumer awareness and little sponsorship history.

Transnet Freight Rail is the freight rail operating division of South African state-owned Transnet, running the national rail network that moves coal, iron ore, manganese, containers, automotive and agricultural freight, notably the export lines to Richards Bay and Saldanha ports. Customers are mining companies, manufacturers and shippers, with annual volumes in the hundreds of millions of tonnes at peak. Wholly owned by the South African government. Critical national infrastructure with low consumer visibility but high public profile because of performance and reform debates.

Vital Farms is a US food company selling pasture-raised eggs and butter under the Vital Farms brand, sourced from a network of several hundred small family farms and certified humane, with products in thousands of stores including Whole Foods, Kroger and Target. Customers are health-conscious US consumers, and revenue is around 500 to 600 million dollars. Founded in 2007 and based in Austin, Texas, and listed on Nasdaq (VITL) since 2020. A growing consumer food brand with strong social media marketing and brand visibility among US households.

Zimbabwe Power Company (ZPC) is a Zimbabwean state-owned electricity generator, a subsidiary of ZESA Holdings, operating the Kariba South hydropower station and the Hwange, Munyati, Harare and Bulawayo thermal power stations. It sells electricity to the national transmission utility, ZETDC, with total capacity of around 1,500 MW when fully operating. Based in Harare. Government-owned B2B utility with no consumer brand, although it is nationally well known.

Advanced Radio Telecom Corp (ART) was a US fixed wireless broadband provider in Bellevue, Washington, that built 38 GHz millimetre wave networks in the late 1990s to deliver high-speed data to businesses in US cities, and later became First Avenue Networks. Customers were business users and telecom carriers. It listed on Nasdaq (ARTT) and went through restructuring, ending as a spectrum holding company. No longer active as an operating brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Alamar Biosciences is a US life sciences tools company that makes the ARGO HT system and NULISA assays for high-sensitivity proteomics, allowing researchers to measure thousands of proteins in tiny samples, aimed at biomarker discovery and early disease detection research, including in Alzheimer's. Customers are academic labs, pharma and biobanks, and revenue comes from instruments and assay kits. Based in Fremont, California, private and venture backed. Known in proteomics circles, with no consumer awareness.

Anagram Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company in Natick, Massachusetts, developing oral enzyme replacement therapy, with a first programme for cystic fibrosis patients with pancreatic insufficiency, aiming to deliver enzymes in capsule form in place of porcine-derived products. It is venture backed and has no approved products. Known only to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record.

Apothecon Pharmaceuticals is an Indian pharmaceutical manufacturer based in Vadodara, Gujarat, making generic formulations such as tablets, capsules and injectables for the domestic and export markets. Crunchbase gives it as a manufacturing and health care company. I cannot confirm specific brands or ownership. A B2B or generic drug maker with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Atavistik Bio is a US biotechnology company developing small-molecule drugs that bind allosteric sites on proteins, discovered with its metabolite-protein interaction mapping platform, aimed at cancer and metabolic diseases. Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, it is private and venture backed, with no approved products. Known only to investors and scientists, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship activity, so it is not a natural F1 brand-sponsor prospect.

Bezeq is Israel's largest telecommunications group, providing fixed-line telephony, broadband internet and fibre, pay TV (via yes), mobile (Pelephone) and international services, and is the owner of much of the country's fixed network. Its customers are Israeli households and businesses, and revenue is several billion shekels. Based in Tel Aviv and listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (BEZQ), with controversy in the past around its ownership. Very well-known consumer and business brand in Israel, with sports sponsorship activity.

Boardwalk REIT is a Canadian real estate investment trust and one of the country's largest multi-family landlords, owning and managing tens of thousands of apartment suites across Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario and Quebec under the Boardwalk Rental Communities brand. Customers are renters, and revenue comes from rents. Based in Calgary and listed on the TSX (BEI.UN). Well known locally in Alberta as a landlord brand, but not a mass consumer brand.

Caspian Networks was a US networking equipment start-up in San Jose that built high-end IP routers for managing multimedia traffic on service provider networks, with a focus on per-flow traffic management. It raised large venture rounds around 2000 to 2005 and failed to scale, shutting down or being sold at a low value. B2B telecom equipment business that no longer operates, with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Ceva Sante Animale is a French veterinary health company, one of the world's largest animal health groups, making vaccines, pharmaceuticals and parasiticides for pets, poultry, pigs, ruminants and other livestock, along with products for pet health and reproduction. Customers are veterinarians, farmers and pet owners in over 100 countries, with revenue of around 1.5 billion euros. Founded in 1999 and based near Bordeaux, it is privately held and owned by founder Marc Prikazsky and partners. Strong B2B brand among vets, with modest consumer recognition.

Cibus is a US agricultural biotechnology company that uses gene editing to develop crop traits, such as herbicide tolerance, disease resistance and yield traits, for rice, canola and other crops, using its Rapid Trait Development System. Customers are seed companies and growers, and it earns through licences and partnerships. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (CBUS) following its 2023 merger with Calyxt. Known to ag-tech investors, with no consumer awareness.

Diagonal Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company developing agonist antibodies that activate cell receptors by controlling how receptor molecules arrange themselves, for diseases such as hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. Based in Watertown, Massachusetts, it is venture backed, with no approved products. Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness or sponsorship track record, so it would be a long shot as a sponsorship prospect.

Expedition Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company in San Francisco developing treatments for COPD and other respiratory diseases, as the Crunchbase text indicates. It is venture backed and has no approved products. I know little beyond that. No consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Foghorn Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing medicines that target the chromatin regulatory system, or the way DNA is packaged and read, with candidates against BRD4, SMARCA2 and other proteins in cancer, and a collaboration with Merck and Lilly. It has no approved products. Founded in 2015, and listed on Nasdaq (FHTX). Known to oncology researchers and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Fore Biotherapeutics is a US precision oncology company in Philadelphia developing targeted therapies, led by plixorafenib (a BRAF inhibitor) for BRAF-mutated cancers such as low-grade glioma and thyroid cancer. It is private and venture backed and has no approved products. Known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship record, so it is an unlikely F1 brand partner.

FreeWire Technologies was a US maker of ultrafast electric vehicle chargers with built-in batteries, such as the Boost Charger, designed to be installed without major grid upgrades at sites like fuel stations, retail locations and fleet depots. Customers were charging network operators, retailers and fleets, and it was backed by BP, Mitsubishi and others. Based in Newark, California, it ceased operations in 2024 after financial difficulty. No consumer brand awareness now.

Generator Hostels is a European hostel and lifestyle accommodation chain, operating design-led hostels with private rooms, dorms, bars and event spaces in cities such as London, Paris, Berlin, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Rome, Copenhagen, Dublin and Venice, plus a few in the US. Customers are young and budget-conscious travellers, and revenue comes from room, food and drink sales. Founded in 1995 and based in London, it was owned by Patron Capital, and acquired in 2019 by Queensgate Investments, a unit of the Qatar Investment Authority group, from Patron. Recognised among backpackers and young travellers across Europe.

INEA is a Polish telecommunications operator based in Poznan that provides broadband internet, cable television, fixed-line and mobile services to homes and businesses, mainly in western Poland (Greater Poland region), using fibre and cable networks. It also sells services to wholesale customers and has grown by acquiring local cable networks. Regional consumer brand in Poland with local recognition around Poznan, and a likely local sponsor of regional sport and events. I cannot confirm ownership or listing details. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Knife River Corporation is a US construction materials and contracting company that mines aggregates (crushed stone, sand and gravel), makes ready-mix concrete and asphalt, and builds roads, bridges and other infrastructure projects across the western and central United States. Customers are state transport departments, contractors and developers, with revenue of around 2.8 billion dollars. Spun off from MDU Resources in 2023 and listed on the NYSE (KNF), with headquarters in Bismarck, North Dakota. B2B, with strong local presence but little consumer brand awareness.

Matchpoint Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing small molecule drugs, with a focus on inflammation and immunology and a partnership with a large pharma company. It launched in 2022 with venture backing and no approved products. I do not recognise much about the pipeline beyond that. No consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Medexus Pharmaceuticals is a specialty pharmaceutical company, listed on the TSX and Nasdaq (MDP), with US operations run from Chicago, that sells rare disease and specialty treatments such as Rasuvo and Metoject (methotrexate auto-injector) for rheumatology, Ixinity for haemophilia B, and Gleolan for brain tumour surgery. Customers are hospitals, specialists and patients in North America. Revenue is around 100 million dollars. Known to prescribers, with little consumer awareness.

Medisolve is a European holding company, based in Milan, that aggregates healthcare technology and services businesses, aiming to build a platform in health tech. It is tagged by Crunchbase as biotechnology and health care. I cannot confirm its portfolio or ownership. It appears to be a private B2B healthcare group with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Merge Labs is a San Francisco company tagged by Crunchbase as biotechnology and data integration, with a description about a single API connecting software. That matches an unrelated software company (Merge, which sells a unified API for integrations), while a separate Merge Labs brain-computer interface venture backed by prominent AI investors also exists. Because the funding total could fit either, I cannot tell which this refers to. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Monteris Medical is a medical device company, based in Minnesota, that makes the NeuroBlate system, a robotic laser probe guided by MRI to ablate brain tumours, epileptic foci and radiation necrosis through a small opening. Customers are neurosurgeons and hospitals, who buy the system and disposable probes. Founded in 2006 in Canada, it is privately held and venture backed. Known among neurosurgeons, with no consumer awareness.

Mystic Invest Holding is a Portuguese holding company in the Porto area, described by Crunchbase as a financial company with interests in hotels and real estate. I cannot confirm which assets it owns or its ownership, though the tags suggest a private investment group with hospitality and property holdings in Portugal. Little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Nouscom is a Swiss-Italian biotechnology company developing cancer vaccines based on viral vectors, with an off-the-shelf approach for tumours with shared antigens and personalised neoantigen vaccines, using Nouscom's proprietary vectors from its Rome lab. Its lead programme targets colorectal cancer. It is private and venture backed, with no approved products. Known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Oryzon Genomics is a Spanish clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing epigenetic drugs, notably iadademstat (an LSD1 inhibitor) for acute myeloid leukaemia and vafidemstat for neuropsychiatric disorders. It earns revenue from licensing, for example with Roche and Jiangsu Hengrui, and from grants. Founded in 2000 and listed on the Spanish Stock Exchange (ORY), headquartered in Barcelona. Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Ray Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in the San Francisco Bay Area developing optogenetic gene therapies to restore vision in patients with retinitis pigmentosa and other inherited retinal diseases, with its lead candidate RTx-015. It is private and venture backed, with no approved products. Known to ophthalmology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record, so it is an unlikely F1 brand partner.

Sensei Biotherapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing cancer immunotherapy, including SNS-101, an antibody targeting VISTA that is active in the acidic tumour environment. It has no approved products and funds trials through equity raises. Listed on Nasdaq (SNSE) since 2021. Known to oncology specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record, so it is an unlikely F1 brand partner.

Senti Biosciences is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company developing gene-circuit cell therapies, engineered immune cells with logic gates that can distinguish cancer cells from healthy ones, led by SENTI-202 for blood cancers. It has no approved products and funds programmes through equity and collaborations. Listed on Nasdaq (SNTI) following a 2022 SPAC merger. Known to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness.

Siegfried Holding is a Swiss contract development and manufacturing organisation for pharmaceuticals, producing active pharmaceutical ingredients, intermediates and finished drug products for pharma companies at sites in Switzerland, Germany, France, Spain, Malta, the US and China. Customers are global drug makers. Founded in 1873, based in Zofingen and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (SFZN), with revenue of around 1.3 billion Swiss francs. Strong B2B brand among pharma companies but unknown to consumers.

THINK Surgical is a US medical robotics company that develops the TSolution One robotic system for knee and hip replacement surgery, which uses a surgeon's 3D plan to guide an active robot that mills the bone. Customers are hospitals, surgeons and surgery centres, who buy the robot and the open implant platform. Based in Fremont, California, it descends from Curexo's Robodoc technology and is backed by a Korean-listed parent. Known to orthopaedic surgeons, with no consumer awareness.

TISSIUM is a French medical device company that develops biodegradable polymer-based sealants and tissue reconstruction products, with a first product, the COAPTIUM CONNECT system for nerve repair, authorised by the US FDA in 2023. Customers are surgeons and hospitals. It was founded in 2013 in Paris as a spin-out from research at MIT and Harvard, and is venture backed. Known to surgeons and medtech investors, with no consumer awareness.

Triveni Bio is a US biotechnology company in Watertown, Massachusetts, developing antibody therapies for inflammatory and fibrotic diseases, especially in dermatology, such as atopic dermatitis, with candidates directed at kallikrein-related targets. It is private and venture backed, with no approved products. Known only to specialists and investors, with no consumer awareness and no sponsorship track record, so it is not a typical F1 sponsorship prospect.

Weights & Biases is a US machine learning developer platform used to track experiments, manage datasets and models, evaluate large language model applications (with its Weave product), and collaborate on AI projects. Customers include OpenAI, Nvidia, Toyota and thousands of AI teams, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2017 in San Francisco and acquired by CoreWeave in 2025 for about 1.7 billion dollars. Well known among AI engineers, with no mass consumer awareness.

Xeltis is a Dutch clinical-stage medical technology company, based in Eindhoven, developing restorative vascular grafts and heart valves made from polymers that guide the body to grow its own tissue, with products such as the aXess vascular access graft for dialysis patients. Customers will be surgeons and hospitals once products are approved. Founded in 2010 as a spin-out of Eindhoven University of Technology and venture backed. Known to medtech specialists, with no consumer awareness.

Afya is a Brazilian medical education company that runs medical schools and also offers continuing education, a digital platform for physicians (Whitebook, Medical Harbour and iClinic software) and clinical services. Customers are medical students, doctors and healthcare institutions, and revenue is mostly tuition. Based in Belo Horizonte, with dozens of campuses across Brazil, and listed on Nasdaq (AFYA) since 2019. Well known among Brazilian medical students and doctors, with modest general consumer awareness.

Centivo is a US digital health plan company offering self-funded employers a primary care-centred health plan, directing members to high-value providers and offering lower-cost care. Customers are mid-size employers who cover their employees' healthcare, and revenue comes from administrative and care management fees. Founded in 2016 and based in Buffalo, New York, it is venture backed. B2B healthcare brand known to benefits advisers and HR teams, with little awareness among the general public.

Enfabrica is a US semiconductor start-up developing networking silicon and software for AI data centres, with its ACF-S chip that combines network switching and memory access to link many GPUs together efficiently. Customers are cloud providers and AI infrastructure builders. Founded in 2020 by former Broadcom and Google engineers and backed by Nvidia, Sutter Hill and Atreides, and based in Mountain View, California. In 2025 Nvidia hired its leadership in a licensing deal. B2B, with niche awareness in AI hardware and none among consumers.

EQuest Education Group is a Vietnamese education company in Ho Chi Minh City, tagged by Crunchbase as education and higher education. It appears to operate private schools or learning programmes for Vietnamese families, with revenue from tuition, and it has attracted around 235 million dollars of investment. I cannot confirm its brands, campuses or ownership. Some recognition among affluent families in Vietnam. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Fotolia was a stock photography marketplace, based in New York with roots in Paris, which sold royalty-free photos, illustrations and videos contributed by a global community of photographers, to designers, agencies and publishers. Founded in 2004, it was bought by Adobe in 2014 for about 800 million dollars and integrated into Adobe Stock, after which the Fotolia brand was retired. Once widely used by creative professionals, it no longer exists as a standalone company.

Kased Khair is an Egyptian construction and general supplies contractor, based in Alexandria, which Crunchbase tags as construction. Its funding is listed at about 12 billion Egyptian pounds, though I cannot confirm what projects it builds, who owns it or its scale. It is likely a B2B contractor serving Egyptian developers and public bodies, with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Makkah Construction and Development Company is a Saudi real estate and hospitality business based in Makkah, which owns and develops hotels and commercial property in the holy city, serving pilgrims and visitors. Revenue comes from hotel operations and rents. It is listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). It is well known in Makkah and has national prominence due to its location, although it is a property owner rather than a consumer brand.

Markley Group is a US data centre and telecommunications infrastructure company, best known for 1 Summer Street in Boston, New England's largest multi-tenant carrier hotel and data centre, plus other facilities in Massachusetts. Customers are carriers, enterprises, cloud providers and the financial sector, paying colocation and interconnection fees. Privately held. B2B brand known in the Boston technology community, with no consumer awareness and no known sponsorship activity.

Novatel Wireless was a US maker of mobile broadband devices, best known for MiFi mobile hotspots, USB modems and embedded wireless modules, sold through carriers such as Verizon, AT&T and Sprint and for machine-to-machine uses. Based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (NVTL), it renamed itself Inseego in 2016 and now focuses on 5G devices and fixed wireless access, with its Inseego Wavemaker subsidiary. The MiFi brand reached consumers, but the name Novatel Wireless has since been retired.

Palm Hills Developments is one of Egypt's leading real estate developers, based in Cairo, building residential compounds, villas and commercial projects such as Palm Hills October, Palm Hills New Cairo, Badya and Hacienda on the north coast. Customers are Egyptian home buyers and expatriates, with revenue from property sales. Founded in 2005 and listed on the Egyptian Exchange (PHDC). Well recognised in the Egyptian property market and with consumer-facing marketing campaigns.

SoftBank Robotics Holdings is the robotics business of SoftBank Group, which developed Pepper, the humanoid social robot, and acquired Aldebaran's NAO. It also offers cleaning, service and delivery robots and robotics software for businesses in Japan and worldwide. Customers are retailers, hotels and facility managers. Based in Tokyo. Pepper was widely known in the 2010s, and the SoftBank name brings strong consumer recognition in Japan, including in sports sponsorship.

SoYoung Technology (New Oxygen) is a Chinese online platform for cosmetic surgery and aesthetic medical services, connecting consumers with clinics and doctors, with reviews, price comparison, consultation and booking. Revenue comes from advertising and service fees paid by medical beauty providers, and from direct sales of treatments. Founded in 2013 and based in Beijing, it listed on Nasdaq (SY) in 2019 as So-Young. Well known among young Chinese consumers interested in cosmetic procedures.

SPH Health Commerce is a Chinese internet hospital and online pharmacy business, a unit of Shanghai Pharmaceuticals, that sells medicines and healthcare products online and provides digital consultation and prescription services, based in Shanghai. Customers are Chinese patients and consumers, with revenue from drug and product sales. I do not recognise the specific entity name in detail, and the group is large and state-linked. Modest consumer recognition via Shanghai Pharmaceuticals brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

TerraPact is a US infrastructure company, based near Boston, that acquires and manages rights-of-way corridor assets such as utility easements, rail corridors and telecom conduit, leasing them to carriers and energy projects. It focuses on critical infrastructure real estate and reports around 240 million dollars of funding. B2B and private, with no consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

UAB Rudina is a Lithuanian construction company from Vilnius, active in the building sector, specifically described by Crunchbase as construction. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Vastned is a Dutch-based retail property investor, listed on Euronext Amsterdam (VASTN), that owns high-street shops in prime shopping streets in Dutch and Belgian cities, as well as in France and Spain earlier. Vero Internet is a Brazilian fibre broadband provider, based in Sao Paulo, that sells fibre-to-the-home internet to residential customers across Brazil under the Vero brand, competing with Vivo, Claro and others. A consumer-health internet brand in China with limited recognition abroad. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Atwell is a US consulting, engineering and construction services firm, based in Southfield, Michigan, offering civil engineering, land development, surveying, environmental, energy and real estate services, with offices across the US. B2B professional services brand, known in the engineering and development community, with limited consumer awareness and no known sponsorship activity.

Bjelin Group is a Swedish flooring company, based in Helsingborg, that develops, manufactures and sells laminate, vinyl and wood flooring under the Bjelin brand and others, with strong sales in Nordic and European markets. Customers are retailers, builders and consumers via DIY stores. Privately held. Moderate brand awareness among flooring buyers in Scandinavia, and mostly a B2B supplier to flooring chains, with little consumer marketing of its own.

CAMH, the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health, is Canada's largest mental health and addiction teaching hospital, based in Toronto, offering clinical care, research and policy work, and affiliated with the University of Toronto. It serves patients across Ontario and runs the Campbell Family Mental Health Research Institute. Funded by government and philanthropy through the CAMH Foundation. A well-known healthcare charity brand in Canada, relevant to mental health awareness partnerships.

Chicago Atlantic Real Estate Finance is a US commercial mortgage real estate investment trust that makes senior secured loans to state-licensed cannabis operators, which cannot access normal bank financing. Its borrowers include multi-state cannabis firms, and revenue comes from interest. Externally managed and based in Chicago, it is listed on Nasdaq (REFI). B2B lender with no consumer brand, and the cannabis exposure limits sponsorship use.

Echo360 is a US education technology company whose platform supports lecture capture, video, active learning and student engagement, used in higher education institutions. Customers are universities and colleges, which pay subscriptions. Founded in 2001, it is a private company. Known among academic technology buyers, with no general consumer awareness. B2B only, so a sponsorship partnership would be unusual and of little commercial logic.

Elite Clinical Network is a US clinical research business, with pharmaceutical research sites for clinical trials, based in Las Vegas, Nevada. Crunchbase tags it as consumer software and health care, and reports funding of about 200 million dollars. I cannot confirm site counts or ownership. B2B service provider to drug sponsors, with limited consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Emirates REIT is a Dubai real estate investment trust listed on Nasdaq Dubai (REIT), owning office, retail and education properties in the UAE, such as Index Tower in DIFC, Loft Offices, Dubai Knowledge Park buildings and student housing in Dubai. Tenants include corporate and government occupiers, and revenue is rental. Managed by Equitativa and has faced debt and valuation challenges. B2B landlord with limited consumer brand awareness.

Fletcher Building is a New Zealand-based building materials and construction group, making and distributing products across brands like Winstone Wallboards, Golden Bay Cement, Laminex, Tasman Insulation, PlaceMakers and Iplex, plus residential development and construction. Customers include builders, tradespeople and DIY buyers in New Zealand and Australia. Listed on the NZX and ASX (FBU), with revenue of about 7 billion New Zealand dollars. Strong household recognition in New Zealand, and a regular sports and event sponsor.

Havea is a French natural health and cosmetics manufacturer, producing herbal supplements, skincare, hygiene and wellness products for pharmacies, retailers and private labels. Customers are retailers, pharmacies and consumers across Europe. Based in Paris. It is mostly a B2B manufacturer with some consumer brands in French pharmacies, and I cannot confirm brand names. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Hayat Holding is a Turkish consumer goods group, whose subsidiaries include Hayat Kimya, a maker of Molfix and Bebem baby diapers, Papia tissue and hygiene paper, and Bingo detergents. It also owns Kastamonu Entegre wood panels. Customers are consumers and retailers across Turkey, Europe, Russia and the Middle East. Strong household brand recognition across Turkey. Privately held, with large mass-market advertising budgets that make it a plausible sponsor in the region.

Kaufman & Broad is a leading French residential property developer, building apartments and houses, offices and commercial properties, and student housing for private buyers and institutions across France. Founded in 1968, as the French arm of the US firm, it is listed on Euronext Paris (KOF) and based in Neuilly-sur-Seine, with revenue of around 1.3 billion euros. Known to French home buyers through its marketing and as a major developer, although it is a B2C/B2B property business and not a mass consumer product brand.

Korea Credit Data (KCD) is a South Korean credit information company, which provides credit data, scoring and analytics for small businesses, based on data from point-of-sale devices, VANs and payments, and offers data products to banks and fintechs. Customers are financial institutions, merchants and policy makers. Based in Seoul, it holds a license as a credit bureau for small and medium business owners. B2B data brand, known in Korean finance, with little consumer awareness.

Metacore is a Finnish mobile games company, based in Helsinki, best known for Merge Mansion, a puzzle game combining merge mechanics with a mystery story, which has been downloaded tens of millions of times and is played worldwide. Revenue comes from in-app purchases and advertising. Supported by large funding rounds and privately held. Strong app store presence, with moderate consumer brand recognition and heavy digital advertising.

Multiconsult is a Norwegian engineering, architecture and consulting firm that provides planning, design and advisory services for buildings, infrastructure, energy, hydropower and the oil and gas sector, with offices across Norway and abroad. Customers are public authorities, developers and industrial firms, with revenue of around 5 billion Norwegian kroner. Founded in 1908 and based in Oslo, it is listed on Oslo Bors (MULTI). B2B professional services brand known in Scandinavian construction, with no mass consumer profile.

The Richman Group is a US affordable housing developer and investor, based in Greenwich, Connecticut, that builds and owns affordable and workforce apartment communities across the US, using low-income housing tax credits. Customers are renters and investors who invest in housing funds, and revenue comes from fees, development and property income. Founded in 1970 by Richard Richman, privately held. B2B brand known to investors and housing agencies, with no consumer awareness.

Tikona Infinet is an Indian broadband provider, based in Mumbai, that offers wireless and fibre broadband internet to homes and enterprises in many cities and small towns, plus enterprise connectivity. Customers are residential and business subscribers. Backed by Indian and international investors. Regional consumer brand with moderate recognition, mainly in Mumbai, Gujarat and other markets, and a modest marketing budget compared with larger Indian telecoms.

TVS Logistics Services is an Indian third-party logistics provider, part of the TVS group, offering supply chain solutions including inbound logistics for automotive, warehousing, distribution, aftermarket parts management and aviation-related services, with operations in India, Europe, the UK and the US. Customers are automotive, retail and consumer brands. Based in Chennai and listed on Indian exchanges (TVSSCS). B2B logistics brand, benefiting from the well-known TVS group name in India.

Vanderbilt Office Properties is a US commercial real estate development, described by Crunchbase as involving Hillwood Urban and TriPost, in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, and is a property project vehicle. I cannot confirm much beyond this and the location is not given. It is a B2B real estate asset with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

XM Radio was a US satellite radio service providing subscription music, news, talk and sports channels to cars and homes, through its own satellites and receivers, with partnerships with General Motors and other carmakers. It had millions of subscribers and was based in Washington DC, and listed on Nasdaq (XMSR). In 2008 it merged with Sirius to form Sirius XM Radio, and the XM brand continues as a service. Strong consumer awareness in North America and a history of broad sports marketing, including NASCAR and major league sports.

Anillo Vial is a private consortium building the Anillo Vial Periferico, a major ring road project around Lima, Peru, as a concession involving large construction groups. It is a single infrastructure project rather than an operating company, and revenue is expected from tolls and government payments. Based in Lima. No consumer brand beyond the road itself. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Betsson is a Swedish online gambling group operating casino, sports betting, poker and bingo brands including Betsson, Betsafe, NordicBet, Casinoeuro and Betsson Sport, in Europe, Latin America and Africa. Customers are consumers across dozens of licensed markets, and revenue is gaming income of around 1 billion euros. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (BETS B). Strong awareness in Nordic and Latin American markets, and a history of major sports sponsorship including football. Gambling sponsorship is restricted in many F1 markets.

Big Hit Music is a South Korean entertainment label, the home of the global K-pop group BTS and later TXT, formerly Big Hit Entertainment, and a subsidiary of HYBE Corporation. It manages artists, produces music and merchandise, and earns revenue from albums, concerts and licensing. Founded in 2005 by Bang Si-hyuk, based in Seoul, and now part of HYBE, which is listed on the Korea Exchange (352820). Huge global fan base through BTS, so strong brand reach, though sponsorship is typically via the artists and HYBE.

ClassDojo is a US education technology company whose free app connects teachers, parents and students for classroom communication, sharing photos and announcements, behaviour feedback and positive reinforcement, used in about 95 percent of US K-8 schools and in over 180 countries. It earns revenue from optional parent subscriptions (ClassDojo Plus) and has a large base of free users. Founded in 2011 and based in San Francisco, it is venture backed by Greylock, GSV and others. Strong brand awareness among teachers and parents, with a friendly monster mascot.

Edly is a US education finance company that offers income-based repayment financing for college students and professionals, funding tuition and programme costs in return for a share of future income, and provides financing to schools and coding bootcamps. Based in New York, it was founded in the 2010s and is private. Customers are students and education providers. I cannot confirm detailed volumes. Little consumer brand awareness beyond its niche. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Eltel was a Northern European provider of technical services for power grids, communications networks and railway infrastructure, with operations in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, Germany and Poland. Customers were utilities, telecom operators and railway owners, and revenue came from installation, maintenance and project contracts. Based in Stockholm and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ELTEL) after a 2015 IPO. It has since been restructured, and I cannot confirm its current ownership. B2B infrastructure contractor with no consumer profile.

EPARK is a Japanese operator of reservation and information platforms for healthcare and services, including EPARK clinic reservation, EPARK pharmacy for prescription ordering, EPARK dental, beauty and gourmet restaurant booking services, used by millions of Japanese users to book appointments online. Customers are clinics, pharmacies, restaurants and consumers, and revenue comes from fees and subscriptions. Based in Tokyo, founded in 1998, and privately held. Strong recognition in Japanese online booking and healthcare, though less known abroad.

EV Cargo is a privately owned global logistics business offering freight forwarding by air, sea and road, contract logistics, warehousing and project cargo, with parcel and haulage operations in the UK. Customers are manufacturers, retailers and shippers. Headquartered in Hong Kong with a large UK base. It is a B2B logistics brand known to shippers, with limited consumer visibility and no sponsorship record I can confirm. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Founders is an Egyptian real estate and property consulting company based in Cairo, tagged by Crunchbase as real estate and real estate investment. It reports large funding of about 10 billion Egyptian pounds, which suggests a major development or investment plan. I cannot confirm what it develops or who owns it. Some recognition in Egypt's property market. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Mivne Group is an Israeli commercial real estate group, based in Tel Aviv, that develops and owns office buildings, logistics centres, shopping centres and mixed-use properties in Israel, and invests abroad. Customers are corporate tenants and retailers. It has been listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Well known in Israeli real estate and finance, but a landlord with little consumer brand profile and no known sponsorship activity.

Paradigm Housing Group is a UK housing association, based in Chesham, Buckinghamshire, that provides social and affordable rented homes, shared ownership, housing for older people and supported housing across the South East of England. Customers are tenants, leaseholders and local authorities, and it is a not-for-profit organisation reinvesting surplus in homes. Owns and manages thousands of homes. Local social housing brand with limited commercial profile and no known sports sponsorship.

Schweiger Dermatology Group is a US dermatology practice network, with clinics across New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Pennsylvania and Florida, offering medical dermatology, cosmetic procedures such as Botox and lasers, and skin cancer surgery. Customers are patients and cosmetic clients. It has dozens of locations and a large workforce of clinicians. Some regional consumer recognition in the New York area. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Tibber is a Norwegian-founded digital electricity supplier that sells power at spot price through a smart app, with smart home controls such as EV charging and heat pump optimisation, and Pulse devices to monitor use. Customers are households in Norway, Sweden, Germany and the Netherlands, who pay a small subscription on top of wholesale prices. Founded in 2016 and venture backed, it is known for its green energy and app-based service. Growing consumer brand in Nordics and Germany with significant digital marketing.

Top Frontier Investment Holdings is a Philippine holding company that controls San Miguel Corporation through its stake of around half, giving it exposure to San Miguel's food and beverage (San Miguel Beer, Ginebra San Miguel, Magnolia), packaging, energy, fuel and infrastructure businesses, as well as banking and airline interests. Controlled by Ramon Ang and associates and based in Makati. Not itself a consumer brand, but the San Miguel group has very strong recognition in the Philippines and a long tradition of sports sponsorship.

Traeger Pellet Grills makes wood pellet grills and smokers that cook with hardwood pellets, plus pellets, rubs, sauces and accessories, and operates the Traeger app and recipes for connected cooking. Customers are US consumers buying through retailers like Home Depot, Lowe's and Costco and online, with revenue near 600 million dollars. Founded in 1985, it is based in Salt Lake City and listed on the NYSE (COOK) since 2021. Strong brand recognition among barbecue enthusiasts in the US, with sponsorships of sports and cooking events.

Union Property Services is a UK property development and services business based in Newcastle upon Tyne, active in commercial property and development. Crunchbase tags it as commercial property and development. I cannot confirm projects, ownership or scale. Likely a regional B2B property business with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Weave Living is a collaborative living company that creates furnished co-living and rental apartments with shared spaces for young professionals, tagged by Crunchbase as communities and coworking. Some recognition among young urban renters. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Regional consumer brand in a few African markets, with limited awareness elsewhere.

Al Mouj Muscat is a large mixed-use waterfront development in Muscat, Oman, featuring residential communities, marinas, a championship golf course (Almouj Golf, which hosts major golf events), retail, hotels and a promenade. It is a property development company serving homebuyers, visitors and golfers, with sales to Omani and foreign buyers. Well known in Oman as a lifestyle destination, with a track record of hosting professional golf tournaments. I cannot confirm shareholders. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

The Austrian Academy of Sciences (OeAW) is Austria's central non-university research institution, funding and running institutes for natural sciences, life sciences, humanities and social sciences, and acting as a learned society that gives out prizes and runs conferences. Not a commercial company, so it has no consumer brand and is not a sponsor target. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Beyond Oblivion is a music and technology company in New York, which Crunchbase tags as legal, mobile and music. Founded in 2006 and based in Boise, Idaho, it was acquired by Ericsson in 2020 for about 1.1 billion dollars and operates as Ericsson Enterprise Wireless Solutions. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Empire Communities is a Canadian home builder and master-planned community developer based in Vaughan, Ontario, building low-rise houses, townhomes and condominium towers in the Greater Toronto Area, and also expanding into Alberta and the US. Customers are home buyers and investors. Privately held and among the larger builders in the Toronto region. Recognised in Ontario housing markets through its marketing, though it is not a mass consumer brand. I cannot confirm sales figures. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Lockall is a French company in Paris tagged by Crunchbase as real estate and rental property, described as offering security and access management solutions. Little verified information. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

NORNORM is a Danish circular furnishing company that offers subscription-based furniture, for homes and offices, with 3D technology to configure products. I know it only in outline. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Stoeffler is a French food company, based in Obernai, Alsace, that makes and sells Alsatian charcuterie, sausages, cooked meats and catering products, supplying supermarkets and food service customers across France. B2B and retail brand with regional recognition in eastern France, and some national shelf presence. I cannot confirm ownership details or its scale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Topia is a US talent mobility platform that helps companies manage global employee moves, relocation, immigration, tax compliance and remote work, with software and advisory services. Customers are large employers and HR teams. Based in San Francisco, and venture and private equity backed. B2B HR technology brand known in global mobility circles, with no consumer awareness and little reason to buy F1 sponsorship, apart from hospitality for corporate clients.

The University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus is a major academic medical centre in Aurora, Colorado, housing schools of medicine, dentistry, nursing, public health and pharmacy, and research institutes, in partnership with UCHealth and Children's Hospital Colorado. Not a typical F1 sponsor.

The University of South Florida is a public research university, with its main campus in Tampa and branches in St Petersburg and Sarasota-Manatee, enrolling around 50,000 students in many programmes, with a large medical school and health sciences. Funding comes from the state, tuition and research grants. Its sports teams, the USF Bulls, compete in the American Athletic Conference. Strong regional brand in Florida, with sports marketing, but not a corporate sponsor.

West Side Square Development Fund is a US real estate development vehicle in Jersey City, New Jersey, set up to fund the West Side Square project, a residential and mixed-use development. It is a single project vehicle formed for investors, not an operating brand. I cannot confirm more. No consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Xiaoe Tech (Xiaoetong) is a Chinese SaaS provider that helps creators and businesses build online courses, memberships and private-traffic stores on WeChat, with live streaming, content sales and AI tools. Customers are knowledge creators, training providers and enterprises, who pay subscriptions and take-rates. Founded in 2014 and based in Shenzhen, it listed in Hong Kong in 2023 (2533). Widely used inside the WeChat ecosystem, with low profile outside China.
